title: Current from charge flow
description: I in amperes when Q coulombs pass a point in t seconds; rearrange as Q = It to find charge.

title: Voltage as work per charge
description: V in volts, W energy in joules, Q charge in coulombs; 1 V = 1 J/C.

title: Electric power
description: P in watts; pick the form that uses the two given quantities (V and I, I and R, or V and R).

title: Electrical energy
description: W in joules when P is in watts and t in seconds; in kWh when P is in kW and t in hours.
plainText: W = P t = V I t

title: Kilowatt-hour to joule
description: Commercial unit of energy (one 'unit' on the bill): 1000 W × 3600 s.

title: Terminal voltage of a practical source
description: E = EMF, r = internal resistance, I = load current; V equals E only at no load, and r = 0 for an ideal voltage source.

title: Resistivity from a sample
description: ρ in Ω·m from the measured resistance R of a sample of length l and cross-sectional area A; classifies the material (conductor ~10⁻⁸, insulator >10¹⁰).

title: Conductivity
description: σ in siemens per metre (S/m); high for conductors (copper ≈ 5.8 × 10⁷ S/m), negligible for insulators.

title: Conductivity from carriers
description: n = free-carrier density (per m³), e = electron charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, μ = mobility (m²/V·s); explains why metals (huge n) conduct and insulators (tiny n) do not.

title: Temperature dependence of resistance
description: α is positive for metals (copper ≈ 0.004/°C), nearly zero for manganin and constantan, negative for semiconductors and insulators.

title: Dielectric strength
description: E_b = dielectric strength (kV/mm), V_b = breakdown voltage, d = insulation thickness; use it to find the voltage a given thickness of insulation can withstand.

title: Series resistance
description: Total resistance of resistors carrying the same current; n equal resistors give nR.

title: Parallel resistance
description: Reciprocals (conductances) add for resistors across the same two nodes; n equal resistors give R/n.

title: Two resistors in parallel
description: Product-over-sum shortcut, valid for exactly two resistors; result is less than the smaller of the two.

title: Voltage divider
description: Voltage across R₁ when R₁ and R₂ are in series across supply V; drops are proportional to resistance.

title: Current divider
description: Current in R₁ when R₁ and R₂ are in parallel carrying total current I; the branch current is proportional to the other branch's resistance.

title: Cells in series and parallel
description: n identical cells of EMF E and internal resistance r; series raises voltage, parallel raises current capacity.
latex: E_s = nE,\; r_s = nr; \qquad E_p = E,\; r_p = \frac{r}{n}
plainText: Series: E_s = nE, r_s = nr ; parallel: E_p = E, r_p = r/n

title: Delta to star: R_A
description: Star resistance at terminal A = product of the two delta resistances meeting at A divided by the sum of all three.

title: Delta to star: R_B and R_C
description: S = R_AB + R_BC + R_CA; same rule applied at terminals B and C.
plainText: R_B = R_AB·R_BC / S ;  R_C = R_BC·R_CA / S

title: Star to delta: R_AB
description: Delta resistance between A and B = sum of the star resistances at A and B plus their product over the third (opposite) star resistance.

title: Star to delta: R_BC and R_CA
description: Same rule for the other two sides of the delta; each uses the star resistance at the opposite terminal as divisor.
latex: R_{BC} = R_B + R_C + \frac{R_B R_C}{R_A}, \quad R_{CA} = R_C + R_A + \frac{R_C R_A}{R_B}
plainText: R_BC = R_B + R_C + R_B·R_C / R_A ;  R_CA = R_C + R_A + R_C·R_A / R_B

title: Star to delta (compact form)
description: Sum of pairwise products of the star resistances divided by the star resistance opposite the side wanted; use R_A for R_BC and R_B for R_CA.
latex: R_{AB} = \frac{R_A R_B + R_B R_C + R_C R_A}{R_C}
plainText: R_AB = (R_A R_B + R_B R_C + R_C R_A) / R_C

title: Balanced networks
description: When all three resistances are equal; star values are one third of delta values.

title: Linearity (superposition) test
description: A circuit is linear when the response to a weighted sum of inputs equals the weighted sum of the individual responses (homogeneity plus additivity).

title: Static and dynamic resistance
description: For a linear element both are equal and constant; for a non-linear element (diode) the dynamic resistance dV/dI varies along the V-I curve.
plainText: R = V / I ;  r = dV / dI

title: Open and short circuit limits
description: Ideal limits used in analysis: an open carries no current, a short has no voltage across it.
plainText: Open: R = ∞, I = 0 ;  Short: R = 0, V = 0

title: Lumped-circuit condition
description: Circuit length l must be much smaller than the wavelength λ (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s); at 50 Hz λ = 6000 km, so power circuits are lumped.

title: Passivity condition
description: Total energy absorbed by a passive element is never negative; an active element can deliver net energy (w < 0).

title: Superposition of responses
description: Total current (or voltage) in an element is the algebraic sum of the partial responses, each found with only one independent source active.

title: Power from superposed current
description: Compute power only after adding the partial currents; the individual powers I'²R and I''²R do not add up to the true power.

title: Current divider
description: Current in R1 when a total current I splits between parallel R1 and R2; used in each single-source step.

title: Thevenin voltage
description: The open-circuit voltage across the load terminals with the load removed and every source active.

title: Thevenin resistance
description: Ratio of open-circuit voltage to short-circuit current at the terminals; equals the dead-network resistance when only independent sources are present.

title: Load current from Thevenin equivalent
description: Current in any load R_L connected to the equivalent; recompute only this line when the load changes.

title: Load voltage from Thevenin equivalent
description: Voltage across the load by voltage division between R_th and R_L.

title: Norton current
description: Current through a short circuit placed across the load terminals with all sources active.

title: Norton resistance
description: Resistance of the dead network seen from the terminals, identical to the Thevenin resistance.

title: Thevenin-Norton conversion
description: Converts between the two equivalents; the resistance stays the same and moves from series to parallel.
plainText: V_th = I_N R_N; I_N = V_th / R_th

title: Load current from Norton equivalent
description: Current-divider rule applied to I_N splitting between R_N and the load R_L.

title: Maximum power condition
description: Load resistance must equal the Thevenin (source) resistance for the load to receive maximum power.

title: Maximum power
description: Power delivered to a matched load; V_th, R_th from the Thevenin equivalent or I_N, R_N from the Norton equivalent.

title: Load power for any R_L
description: General load power; differentiate with respect to R_L to prove the theorem.

title: Efficiency of power transfer
description: Fraction of the total generated power that reaches the load; equals 0.5 (50 %) at R_L = R_th.

title: AC conjugate matching
description: Load impedance for maximum power from an AC source with Thevenin impedance R_th + jX_th; use |Z_th| if the load must be resistive.

title: Inductive reactance
description: Opposition of an inductor L (henry) at frequency f (Hz); grows with frequency, zero for DC.

title: Capacitive reactance
description: Opposition of a capacitor C (farad) at frequency f; falls with frequency, infinite for DC.

title: Series impedance
description: Magnitude of the series impedance; drop the missing term for an R-L or R-C circuit.

title: Phase angle and power factor
description: φ is the angle by which current lags (positive) or leads (negative) the voltage; cos φ is the power factor.
plainText: tan φ = (XL − XC)/R; cos φ = R/Z

title: Time constants
description: Time for a switched R-L or R-C circuit to reach 63.2 % of its final change; in seconds when L in H, C in F, R in Ω.

title: Exponential rise to a final value
description: Current in an R-L circuit or capacitor voltage in an R-C circuit after switching on a DC source at t = 0.

title: Resonant frequency
description: Frequency at which X_L = X_C for any L-C combination; L in henry, C in farad, f in hertz.

title: Quality factor
description: Sharpness of a series resonance and the voltage magnification across L or C at f_r.

title: Bandwidth
description: Width between the half-power frequencies where current is 70.7 % of maximum; narrower for higher Q.

title: Voltage magnification
description: Voltage across the inductor or capacitor of a series circuit at resonance; can be many times the supply voltage.

title: Dynamic impedance (parallel resonance)
description: Purely resistive impedance of a coil (L with series resistance R) in parallel with C at resonance; the line current is V/Z_r.

title: Active power
description: Real power in watts consumed by the load; V and I are rms values and φ the angle between them.

title: Reactive power
description: Power in VAR exchanged with the fields of L and C; positive (lagging) for inductive, negative (leading) for capacitive loads.

title: Apparent power and power triangle
description: Total power in VA that the source must supply; the hypotenuse of the power triangle.

title: Power factor
description: Ratio of active to apparent power (or of resistance to impedance); 1 for pure R, 0 for pure L or C.

title: Capacitor for power-factor correction
description: Reactive power and capacitance of the parallel capacitor that raises the pf from cos φ1 to cos φ2 at supply voltage V and frequency f.
plainText: Q_C = P (tan φ1 − tan φ2); C = Q_C / (2πfV²)

title: Faraday's law of induction
description: Induced EMF e in a coil of N turns equals the rate of change of the flux Φ (weber) linking it; the minus sign is Lenz's law.

title: Motional EMF in a conductor
description: EMF in a conductor of length l moving at velocity v through flux density B when the velocity makes angle θ with the field; e = Blv for perpendicular motion.
plainText: e = B l v sin θ

title: EMF of a rotating coil
description: Instantaneous EMF of an N-turn coil of area A rotating at ω rad/s in a uniform field B, with time measured from the position of maximum flux linkage.
plainText: e = N B A ω sin(ωt) = Em sin(ωt)

title: Peak generated EMF
description: Peak value of the sinusoidal EMF from turns N, flux density B, coil area A and frequency f; divide by √2 for the RMS value.
plainText: Em = N B A ω = 2π f N B A

title: Frequency of an alternator
description: Generated frequency in Hz from the number of poles P and the speed N in rpm; use N = 120f/P to find the speed needed for a given frequency.

title: RMS value of a sinusoid
description: Effective (heating) value of a sine wave from its peak Vm; use RMS in all power calculations and for meter readings.

title: Average value of a sinusoid
description: Mean of a sine wave over one half cycle (the full-cycle mean is zero); used for rectifier output and moving-coil meter deflection.

title: Form factor
description: Ratio of RMS to average value, 1.11 for a sine wave; it converts an average-reading meter scale to RMS.

title: Peak (crest) factor
description: Ratio of peak to RMS value, √2 for a sine wave; gives the peak voltage that insulation and capacitors must withstand.

title: General RMS definition
description: Root of the mean of the squared instantaneous values over one period T; use it for any waveform when the sine-wave factors do not apply.

title: Star connection
description: Line and phase relations for a star (Y) connection; the line voltage leads the corresponding phase voltage by 30° and a neutral point exists.

title: Delta connection
description: Line and phase relations for a delta (Δ) connection; the line current lags the corresponding phase current by 30° and there is no neutral.

title: Three-phase active power
description: Total active power of a balanced load in watts; φ is the angle between phase voltage and phase current and the formula holds for star and delta.
plainText: P = √3 V_L I_L cos φ = 3 V_ph I_ph cos φ

title: Three-phase reactive and apparent power
description: Reactive power in VAR and apparent power in VA of a balanced three-phase load; S = √(P² + Q²) and cos φ = P/S.
plainText: Q = √3 V_L I_L sin φ,  S = √3 V_L I_L

title: Two-wattmeter power factor
description: Power factor angle of a balanced load from the two wattmeter readings W1 and W2; the total power is always W1 + W2.

title: Mass-Action Law
description: n and p are the electron and hole concentrations and ni the intrinsic concentration (1.5 × 10^10 per cm³ for Si at 300 K); holds in thermal equilibrium for any doping.

title: Majority and Minority Concentrations
description: For n-type material with donor density ND much larger than ni; for p-type swap the roles using the acceptor density NA.

title: Semiconductor Conductivity
description: q = 1.6 × 10^-19 C; mu_n and mu_p are the electron and hole mobilities; resistivity is rho = 1/sigma.

title: Drift Velocity
description: Average carrier velocity in an electric field E; the mobility mu is in cm²/(V·s) or m²/(V·s).

title: Diode (Shockley) Equation
description: IS is the reverse saturation current, VT the thermal voltage (26 mV at 300 K) and n the ideality factor (1 to 2); gives the full forward and reverse V-I curve.

title: Thermal Voltage
description: k = 1.38 × 10^-23 J/K, q = 1.6 × 10^-19 C, T in kelvin; about 26 mV at room temperature.
plainText: VT = kT / q ~ 26 mV at 300 K

title: Diode Dynamic Resistance
description: AC (small-signal) resistance of a forward-biased diode at DC current ID; about 26 ohm at 1 mA for n = 1.

title: Zener Regulator Currents
description: Series-resistor Zener regulator: the resistor current splits between the Zener and the load; IZ must stay above the knee current for regulation.

title: BJT Current Relation
description: Kirchhoff's current law applied to the transistor; the emitter carries the sum of base and collector currents.

title: Beta from Alpha
description: Common-emitter gain from common-base gain; alpha = 0.99 gives beta = 99.

title: Alpha from Beta
description: Common-base gain from common-emitter gain; always slightly less than 1.

title: Emitter Current from Base Current
description: Use when IE or IB is given together with beta; 1 + beta is also the common-collector current gain.

title: Collector-Emitter Leakage
description: Leakage with the base open is the collector-base leakage amplified by 1 + beta; total IC = beta IB + ICEO.

title: MOSFET Saturation Current (Square Law)
description: Drain current when VGS > VT and VDS >= VGS - VT; k is the device constant in A/V² and VT the threshold voltage.

title: MOSFET Device Constant
description: mu_n is the channel mobility, Cox the gate-oxide capacitance per unit area and W/L the channel width-to-length ratio; some texts write the same constant as K/2 or kn'(W/L)/2.

title: MOSFET Ohmic-Region Current
description: Valid for VGS > VT and VDS < VGS - VT; for very small VDS the device behaves as a resistor.

title: MOSFET Transconductance
description: Small-signal gain parameter in saturation, the slope of the transfer characteristic; the voltage gain of a common-source stage is about -gm RD.

title: MOSFET On-Resistance
description: Channel resistance deep in the ohmic region (small VDS); a larger gate overdrive gives a lower on-resistance switch.

title: CMOS Dynamic Power
description: Switching power of a CMOS node with load capacitance C, supply VDD and switching frequency f; linear in f, quadratic in VDD.

title: Total CMOS Power
description: Static (leakage) term plus dynamic term; alpha is the activity factor, the fraction of clock cycles in which the node switches.
plainText: P = VDD I_leak + alpha C VDD^2 f

title: Logic Noise Margins
description: High and low noise margins from the output and input threshold levels; CMOS margins are roughly 30 % of VDD, TTL margins about 0.4 V.
latex: NM_H = V_{OH} - V_{IH}, \quad NM_L = V_{IL} - V_{OL}
plainText: NM_H = VOH - VIH;   NM_L = VIL - VOL

title: Dynamic emitter resistance
description: I_E is the DC emitter current at the Q-point; with I_E in mA the result is in ohms, and the base sees β r_e.

title: Transconductance
description: V_T = kT/q ≈ 26 mV at 300 K; g_m is the slope of the I_C–V_BE curve at the Q-point and equals 1 / r_e.

title: Hybrid-π input resistance
description: Resistance seen between base and emitter in the small-signal model; it is the same quantity as h_ie and approximately β r_e.

title: CE small-signal voltage gain
description: Gain of a common-emitter stage with the emitter bypassed; R_C should be replaced by R_C ∥ R_L when a load is connected, and the minus sign marks the 180° phase inversion.

title: DC load line
description: Straight line between cut-off (I_C = 0, V_CE = V_CC) and saturation (V_CE = 0, I_C = V_CC / R_C); the Q-point lies where the bias circuit puts it on this line.

title: Barkhausen criterion
description: A is the amplifier gain and β the feedback fraction; both must hold at the oscillation frequency for sustained sinusoidal output.

title: Gain with positive feedback
description: Closed-loop gain of an amplifier with positive feedback; it tends to infinity as Aβ approaches 1, meaning an output exists with zero input.

title: Start-up condition
description: The loop gain is designed a few percent above unity so that noise at the selected frequency builds up; non-linearity then reduces it to exactly 1.

title: Tank (LC) resonant frequency
description: Natural frequency of a parallel L-C tank (L in henry, C in farad); the frequency at which X_L = X_C and the tank impedance is maximum.

title: Quality factor of a tank
description: r is the series resistance of the coil; a higher Q gives a sharper resonance, a purer sine wave and better frequency stability.

title: Phase-shift oscillator frequency
description: Three identical RC sections each shifting 60°; R in ohm and C in farad give f in hertz.

title: Phase-shift oscillator gain
description: Minimum inverting-amplifier gain, because the three-section RC network attenuates the signal to 1/29 at the oscillation frequency.

title: Wien bridge frequency
description: Lead-lag network with equal R and C in both arms; at this frequency the network has 0° phase shift and attenuation 1/3.

title: Wien bridge gain condition
description: Non-inverting op-amp gain must equal 3 to cancel the 1/3 attenuation; in practice R_f is slightly larger or non-linear for start-up and amplitude control.

title: Wien network with unequal arms
description: General Wien bridge frequency when the series arm (R_s, C_s) and parallel arm (R_p, C_p) differ; reduces to 1/(2πRC) for equal values.

title: Hartley oscillator frequency
description: L_1 and L_2 are the two coil sections and M their mutual inductance (0 if uncoupled); C is the single tank capacitor.

title: Colpitts oscillator frequency
description: C_1 and C_2 are the two series tank capacitors (their series equivalent C_T is smaller than either) and L is the single inductor.

title: Clapp oscillator frequency
description: C_3 is the small capacitor in series with L; since C_3 is much smaller than C_1 and C_2, f ≈ 1/(2π√(LC_3)) and transistor capacitances barely matter.

title: Tank Q and bandwidth
description: r is the coil resistance and BW the half-power bandwidth of the tank; a higher Q gives a purer sine wave and better frequency stability.

title: Crystal series resonance
description: L and C_s are the motional inductance and capacitance of the equivalent circuit; at f_s the crystal impedance is minimum (approximately R).

title: Crystal parallel resonance
description: C_M is the mounting (holder) capacitance; since C_s is much smaller than C_M, f_p is only slightly above f_s and the crystal is inductive between the two.

title: Crystal Q factor
description: R is the motional (loss) resistance; typical quartz values give Q between 10^4 and 10^6, the reason for its excellent frequency stability.

title: Frequency drift from a ppm rating
description: Converts a stability specification in parts per million into hertz; for example 10 MHz at ±20 ppm drifts by at most ±200 Hz.

title: 555 astable frequency
description: R_A is between V_CC and the discharge pin, R_B between the discharge and threshold pins, C the timing capacitor; the period is T = 0.693(R_A + 2R_B)C.

title: 555 astable duty cycle
description: Fraction of the period for which the output is high; always above 50 percent in the basic circuit because C discharges through R_B alone.

title: 555 monostable pulse width
description: Output high time after a trigger; C charges from 0 to 2/3 V_CC through R, independent of the trigger duration and of the supply voltage.

title: BJT astable multivibrator period
description: R_1 and R_2 are the base resistors and C_1 and C_2 the cross-coupling capacitors; each half-period is 0.69RC.

title: UJT relaxation oscillator frequency
description: η is the intrinsic stand-off ratio of the UJT (0.5 to 0.8); R and C are the charging resistor and capacitor; the capacitor voltage is a sawtooth.

title: Schmitt trigger trip points
description: Inverting op-amp Schmitt trigger with R_1 from the output and R_2 to ground feeding the non-inverting input; the two trip points differ by the hysteresis 2βV_sat.
plainText: VUT = +β·Vsat, VLT = −β·Vsat, β = R2/(R1 + R2); hysteresis VH = 2·β·Vsat

title: Voltage and current gain in dB
description: Use for any ratio of voltages or currents; 20 appears because power is proportional to the square of these quantities.

title: Power gain in dB
description: P_o and P_i are output and input signal powers; a power ratio of 2 is 3 dB and of 10 is 10 dB.

title: Bandwidth and half-power points
description: f_L and f_H are the lower and upper cut-off frequencies where gain is 3 dB (a factor 0.707) below the mid-band value A_mid.

title: Efficiency and dissipation
description: P_ac is signal power in the load, P_dc = V_CC × average supply current, and P_D is the heat dissipated in the output device.
plainText: η = P_ac / P_dc × 100 %; P_D = P_dc − P_ac

title: Cascaded stages
description: Linear gains of stages in cascade multiply while decibel gains add; each A_k must be measured with the following stage as its load.
latex: A_T = A_1 A_2 \cdots A_n, \quad A_T(\text{dB}) = \sum A_k(\text{dB})
plainText: A_total = A1 × A2 × ... × An; A_total(dB) = A1(dB) + A2(dB) + ...

title: DC load line
description: Locus of all (V_CE, I_C) operating points for supply V_CC and load R_L; it meets the axes at V_CE = V_CC and I_C = V_CC/R_L.

title: Class A Q-point (series-fed)
description: Centre of the load line, giving the largest symmetrical swing; I_CQ flows continuously even with no signal.

title: Class B supply current
description: Average current drawn from the supply by a class B push-pull pair when the peak load current is I_m; it is zero with no signal.

title: Class D average output
description: Average of the PWM output of a single-supply switching stage; the duty cycle D follows the input signal and the LC filter extracts this average.
plainText: V_o(avg) = D × VCC, D = t_on / T

title: Class A efficiency, series-fed
description: Resistive (RC-coupled) load with Q at the centre of the load line: peak swing V_CC/2 and I_CQ, constant P_dc = V_CC I_CQ.

title: Class A efficiency, transformer coupled
description: No DC drop across the load, so the collector swings the full V_CC and the AC power doubles for the same DC input.

title: Class B efficiency
description: V_m is the peak output voltage of a push-pull pair fed from V_CC; the maximum occurs when V_m = V_CC.

title: Transistor dissipation
description: Power turned into heat in the output device(s); for class A with no signal P_D = V_CC I_CQ, its maximum.

title: Class B maximum dissipation
description: Worst-case total dissipation of a class B push-pull pair (half in each transistor), occurring at 63.7 % of full swing and equal to about 0.4 of the maximum load power.
plainText: P_D(max) = 2 VCC² / (π² RL) at Vm = 2 VCC/π

title: Class AB bias voltage
description: Voltage held between the two bases of a complementary pair so that both transistors are just conducting at zero signal.

title: V_BE multiplier
description: R1 from collector to base and R2 from base to emitter of the bias transistor; the network acts as an adjustable, temperature-tracking diode.

title: Quiescent current with emitter resistors
description: V_BE(Q) is each output transistor's base-emitter voltage at the quiescent point and R_E is each emitter resistor; use it to set or check I_Q.

title: Standby dissipation
description: Heat produced with no signal by a class AB pair running from ±V_CC supplies (V_CC I_Q with a single supply), shared equally by the two transistors.

title: Inverting amplifier gain
description: Closed-loop gain of an inverting op-amp: R_f is the feedback resistor and R_in the input resistor; the minus sign shows the output is 180° out of phase.

title: Non-inverting amplifier gain
description: Closed-loop gain of a non-inverting op-amp, where R_1 runs from the inverting input to ground; the gain is never less than 1 (R_f = 0 gives the voltage follower).

title: Integrator output
description: Op-amp integrator with R at the inverting input and C in the feedback path; a constant input produces a linearly ramping output of slope −V_in / RC.

title: Summing amplifier output
description: Each input feeds the virtual-ground node through its own resistor, so the output is the inverted weighted sum; equal resistors give a plain inverted sum.

title: Slew-rate frequency limit
description: Highest frequency at which a sinusoid of peak V_p can be reproduced without slew distortion; for a 741 (0.5 V/µs) and V_p = 10 V it is about 8 kHz.

title: Junction temperature
description: T_A is the ambient temperature, P_D the dissipated power and θ_JA the total junction-to-ambient thermal resistance (°C/W); the junction must stay below T_J(max).

title: Maximum allowable dissipation
description: The derating rule: allowed power falls linearly as ambient temperature rises, and a heat sink increases it by lowering θ_JA.

title: Reflected load resistance
description: Resistance seen at the transformer primary (per half-primary in push-pull) for a secondary load R_L; used to match a low-impedance speaker to the transistor.

title: Class B push-pull maximum output power
description: Ideal sinusoidal output power when each collector swings the full V_CC into the reflected load R_L'; the corresponding efficiency is π/4 = 78.5 %.

title: Resonant frequency of the tank
description: L in henries and C in farads (including device and stray capacitance) give f_0 in hertz; the tank impedance is maximum and resistive at this frequency.

title: Bandwidth of a tuned amplifier
description: The 3 dB bandwidth between the half-power frequencies f_1 and f_2; Q is the loaded quality factor of the tank, so a higher Q means a narrower, more selective response.

title: Dynamic impedance at resonance
description: Purely resistive impedance of a parallel LC tank with coil series resistance R at f_0; it is the load that sets the gain A_v = −g_m Z_D.

title: Quality factor of the coil
description: Ratio of coil reactance to its series resistance at resonance; loading by the transistor and the next stage lowers the effective Q and widens the band.

title: Ohm's law and power (all forms)
description: V in volts, I in amperes, R in ohms, P in watts; any one form of P follows from V = IR.
latex: V = IR,\qquad P = VI = I^2 R =  rac{V^2}{R}
plainText: V = IR;  P = VI = I²R = V²/R

title: Maximum power transfer
description: Load matched to the Thevenin resistance; efficiency is then only 50 %.

title: Series resonance trio
description: L in henries, C in farads; at f_r the impedance equals R and the power factor is 1.
latex: f_r =  rac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}},\qquad Q =  rac{X_L}{R},\qquad BW =  rac{f_r}{Q}

title: Sine-wave values
description: V_m is the peak value; the average is taken over a half cycle.
plainText: V_rms = 0.707 V_m;  V_avg = 0.637 V_m (half cycle);  form factor 1.11

title: BJT current gains
description: α = I_C/I_E (just below 1) and β = I_C/I_B (tens to hundreds).

title: 555 timer and class B efficiency
description: R in ohms and C in farads give f in hertz and T in seconds; 78.5 % is π/4.
plainText: 555 astable f = 1.44/((R_A + 2R_B)C);  monostable T = 1.1 RC;  class B max efficiency 78.5 %

title: Ohm's law
description: V in volts, I in amperes, R in ohms; valid for ohmic conductors at constant temperature.

title: Resistance of a conductor
description: ρ = resistivity (Ω·m), l = length (m), A = cross-sectional area (m²); use for wires, cables and heating elements.

title: Conductance and conductivity
description: G in siemens (S), σ in S/m; conductances of parallel branches add directly.

title: Resistance at temperature t
description: R₀ = resistance at 0 °C, α₀ = temperature coefficient at 0 °C (per °C), t in °C; α₀ is positive for metals.

title: Resistance between two temperatures
description: Use when the known resistance R₁ is at a temperature t₁ other than 0 °C; α₁ is the coefficient at t₁.

title: Temperature coefficient at t
description: Converts the 0 °C coefficient to its value at t °C; for copper 0.00427 at 0 °C becomes 0.00393 at 20 °C.

title: Kirchhoff's current law
description: At any node the currents entering equal the currents leaving; use it to write node equations.

title: Kirchhoff's voltage law
description: Round any closed loop the rises (EMFs) equal the drops (IR); use it to write loop or mesh equations.
plainText: ΣV = 0 round a loop, i.e. ΣE = ΣIR

title: Source transformation
description: A voltage source V_s in series with R_s equals a current source I_s in parallel with the same R_s; arrow toward the + terminal.

title: Number of independent equations
description: For a circuit with n nodes and b branches; tells you how many node or mesh equations you must write.
plainText: KCL equations = n − 1; KVL equations = b − n + 1

title: Instantaneous value of AC
description: Instantaneous voltage v at time t from peak value Vm, angular frequency ω = 2πf and phase angle φ; the same form gives i = Im sin(ωt + φ).

title: Frequency and time period
description: Frequency f in hertz is the reciprocal of the time period T in seconds; 50 Hz corresponds to T = 20 ms.

title: Angular frequency
description: Angular frequency ω in rad/s from frequency f or period T; equals 314.16 rad/s for 50 Hz.

title: Phase angle from time shift
description: Converts a time displacement Δt between two waves of period T into a phase difference φ; use 360° for degrees or ω for radians.

title: BJT Current Gains
description: Common-emitter gain beta (typically 50 to 300) and common-base gain alpha (slightly less than 1) of a BJT in the active region.
plainText: beta = IC / IB;   alpha = IC / IE

title: Alpha-Beta Conversion
description: Converts between the two BJT current gains; both relations follow from IE = IB + IC.
plainText: alpha = beta / (1 + beta);   beta = alpha / (1 - alpha)

title: Barkhausen criterion
description: A is the amplifier gain and β the feedback fraction; both conditions must hold at the oscillation frequency for a steady sinusoidal output.

title: LC tank resonant frequency
description: L in henry and C in farad give f0 in hertz; use the equivalent L_T or C_T of the tank for Hartley, Colpitts and Clapp oscillators.

title: Voltage gain in dB
description: V_o and V_i are the output and input voltage amplitudes; the same 20 log rule applies to current gain, and a negative result means attenuation.

title: Power gain in dB
description: P_o and P_i are the output and input signal powers; use 10 log because power is proportional to the square of voltage.

title: True length of a line
description: True length from the top-view length and the difference in heights of the two ends above HP.

title: Foreshortened projections
description: Projected lengths of a line inclined at theta to HP and phi to VP.
plainText: Ltop = TL cos(theta), Lfront = TL cos(phi)

title: Isometric scale
description: Foreshortening factor applied to every isometric line in an isometric projection.

title: View to projection ratio
description: An isometric view drawn with true lengths is about 22.5% larger than the isometric projection.

title: Section ellipse of cylinder
description: True shape of the section of a vertical cylinder cut by a plane inclined at theta to HP.
plainText: Major axis = D / cos(theta), minor axis = D

title: True length on cutting plane
description: Recovers true lengths of the section from their foreshortened top-view lengths.

title: Net present value
description: Sum of all net cash flows discounted to time 0 at the MARR; accept if NPV is zero or positive.
plainText: NPV = sum over t = 0..n of CF_t / (1 + i)^t

title: IRR by linear interpolation
description: Estimates the rate at which NPV = 0 from a positive NPV1 at i1 and a negative NPV2 at i2.

title: Simple payback period
description: Years to recover the investment from undiscounted equal annual inflows.
plainText: Payback = initial investment / uniform annual net inflow

title: Benefit-cost ratio
description: Public-project criterion; the project is justified when the ratio is 1 or more.
plainText: B/C = PW of benefits / PW of costs

title: Annual worth
description: Equivalent uniform annual worth of an alternative over its own life, used to compare unequal lives.
plainText: AW = −P(A/P, i, n) + S(A/F, i, n) − AOC

title: Capitalised cost
description: Present worth of a perpetual project: initial cost plus perpetual annual cost divided by the interest rate.

title: Incremental B/C
description: Justifies the costlier alternative 2 over alternative 1 when the ratio is 1 or more.

title: Straight-line depreciation
description: Equal annual depreciation of first cost less salvage over the useful life.

title: Declining-balance book value
description: Book value after t years when a fixed rate d is applied to the opening book value each year (d = 2/n for DDB).

title: Sum-of-years-digits depreciation
description: Accelerated depreciation in year t using the remaining life divided by the sum of the years' digits.

title: After-tax cash flow
description: Cash flow after income tax, where tax is charged on before-tax cash flow less depreciation.

title: Forward and backward pass
description: Earliest finish adds the duration to earliest start; latest start subtracts it from latest finish.
latex: EF = ES + t,\quad LS = LF - t
plainText: EF = ES + t; LS = LF − t

title: Total float
description: Time an activity can slip without delaying project completion; zero on the critical path.

title: Free float
description: Delay an activity can absorb without delaying the earliest start of any successor.

title: Crash cost slope
description: Extra direct cost per unit time saved; crash the critical activity with the lowest slope first.
plainText: Cost slope = (Crash cost − Normal cost) / (Normal time − Crash time)

title: PERT expected time
description: Weighted mean of optimistic, most likely (weight 4) and pessimistic times from the beta distribution.

title: Activity standard deviation
description: One-sixth of the range between pessimistic and optimistic times; its square is the variance.

title: Probability of completion
description: Standard normal value for a scheduled time T_s; read the probability from the normal table.

title: Average resource demand
description: Total resource-days divided by project duration; the target level of a well-smoothed histogram.
plainText: Average resource demand = Σ(r_i × t_i) / T

title: Burgess levelling criterion
description: The schedule with the smallest sum of squared daily demands has the most uniform resource histogram.
plainText: Minimise Σ R_d² over all days

title: Cost and schedule variance
description: Negative CV means over budget; negative SV means less work done than planned.
latex: CV = EV - AC,\quad SV = EV - PV
plainText: CV = EV − AC; SV = EV − PV

title: Performance indices
description: Values below 1 show cost overrun (CPI) or schedule delay (SPI).

title: Estimate at completion
description: Forecast of total cost assuming the current cost efficiency continues to the end.

title: Earned value
description: Budgeted value of the work actually performed to the status date.

title: Risk exposure
description: Expected loss from a single risk, used to rank risks and size reserves.

title: Expected monetary value
description: Probability-weighted value of all outcomes of a decision or chance node.

title: Contingency reserve
description: Budget set aside for identified (known-unknown) risks based on their total expected value.
plainText: Contingency reserve = sum of probability x impact over identified threats

title: Weighted average cost of capital
description: Average after-tax cost of all capital, often used as the project discount rate.

title: Debt-equity ratio
description: Measures financial leverage; a 70:30 structure gives D/E = 2.33.

title: After-tax cost of debt
description: Interest is tax-deductible, so the effective cost of debt is reduced by the tax rate.
plainText: After-tax cost of debt = Rd (1 - T)

title: QCBS combined score
description: Quality and cost based selection score for two-envelope proposals; the lowest price gets a financial score of 100.
latex: S = w_t S_t + w_f S_f,\quad S_f = 100 \times \frac{F_{\min}}{F}
plainText: S = wt St + wf Sf, where Sf = 100 x Fmin / F

title: Bid variation from estimate
description: Compares a bid price B with the approved cost estimate E; negative values are below estimate.

title: Liquidated damages
description: Amount deducted from the contractor for late completion not covered by an extension of time.
plainText: LD = LD rate per day x days of unexcused delay, not exceeding the cap

title: Retention money
description: Sum withheld from each running bill as security for completion and remedying defects.
plainText: Retention = retention percentage x gross interim payment

title: Cost-plus-incentive fee
description: Contractor's fee rises with cost savings and falls with overruns according to the agreed share ratio.
plainText: Fee = target fee + contractor share x (target cost - actual cost)

title: Weighted decision score
description: Scores each option in an ethical or technical decision by weighting its rating on each criterion.

title: Risk exposure
description: Probability times impact, used to judge how serious a safety concern is before deciding to escalate it.

title: Seismic base shear
description: Equivalent static design base shear equals the code's design coefficient times the building's seismic weight.

title: Code compliance rate
description: Share of inspected buildings or items that meet the code, used to monitor enforcement.

title: Frequency rate
description: Number of lost-time injuries per million man-hours worked.

title: Severity rate
description: Man-days lost due to injuries per million man-hours worked.

title: Incidence rate
description: Injuries per thousand workers in the period.

title: Frequency severity index
description: Combines frequency and severity into one index for comparing safety performance.

title: Compound annual growth rate
description: Average yearly growth rate of a quantity such as membership over t years.

title: Participation rate
description: Share of members taking part in an event or programme, a simple indicator of engagement.

title: Registration eligibility
description: A recognised qualification, success in the licensing exam and a complete application together lead to registration.
plainText: Eligibility = recognised degree + licensing exam pass + application

title: Keeping registration valid
description: Registration stays valid only while it is renewed and not suspended or removed by the Council.
latex: \text{Valid registration} = \text{entry in register} + \text{timely renewal} - \text{removal or suspension}
plainText: Valid registration = entry in register + timely renewal - removal or suspension

title: Proportional penalty
description: Minor first breaches draw a warning, while serious or repeated misconduct can lead to suspension or removal.
plainText: Severity of penalty is proportional to gravity of misconduct x repetition

title: Natural justice steps
description: A valid disciplinary process tells the engineer the charges, hears the defence, records reasons and allows appeal.
plainText: Fair discipline = notice + hearing + reasoned decision + appeal

title: Compound amount
description: Future value of a single present sum P after n periods at interest i per period.

title: Net present value
description: Discount every cash flow at the MARR; accept the project when NPV is zero or positive.

title: Straight-line depreciation
description: P first cost, S salvage value and n useful life; the charge is the same every year.

title: PERT expected time
description: a optimistic, m most likely and b pessimistic durations, from the beta distribution.

title: Performance indices
description: Values below 1 mean the project is over budget (CPI) or behind schedule (SPI).

title: Representative fraction
description: Scale expressed as a pure ratio with both lengths in the same unit.
plainText: RF = length on drawing / actual length

title: Length of scale
description: Length to draw a plain or diagonal scale that must measure up to a given maximum length.
plainText: Length of scale = RF x maximum length

title: A-series sheet area
description: Each A-series size has half the area of the previous one, starting from 1 m^2 for A0.

title: Compound amount
description: Future value of a single present amount P after n periods at interest rate i per period.

title: Effective annual rate
description: Converts a nominal annual rate r compounded m times a year into the rate actually earned per year.

title: Uniform-series present worth
description: Present worth at time 0 of n equal end-of-period amounts A.

title: Capital recovery
description: Equal annual amount that recovers a present investment P with interest over n periods, e.g. a loan instalment.

title: Sinking fund
description: Equal end-of-period deposit needed to accumulate a future sum F in n periods.

title: Triple constraint
description: Scope, time and cost are interdependent; changing one affects the others and the achievable quality.

title: WBS 100% rule
description: The work packages of a WBS together must cover all of the project scope and nothing outside it.
plainText: Project scope = sum of all work packages

title: Percent complete
description: Share of the total budgeted work actually accomplished, a standard PMIS dashboard figure.

title: Expected value of perfect information
description: Upper limit on what is worth paying for additional information before a decision.
latex: EVPI = EV_{\text{with perfect info}} - EMV_{\text{best without info}}
plainText: EVPI = expected value with perfect information - best EMV without information

title: Performance indices
description: Cost and schedule efficiency indicators routinely reported by a PMIS; values below 1 signal trouble.
plainText: CPI = EV / AC, SPI = EV / PV

title: GHG emission estimate
description: Emissions equal the activity quantity (e.g. litres of fuel, kWh) multiplied by its emission factor.

title: Impact significance score
description: In matrix methods such as the Leopold matrix, an impact's significance is rated from its magnitude and its importance.

title: Total matrix impact
description: Summing the scores of all activity-environment interactions gives an overall score for comparing alternatives.

title: Right to practise
description: A qualification alone is not enough; registration with the Council gives the legal right to practise in Nepal.
plainText: Legal right to practise = recognised degree + NEC registration

title: Three core roles
description: The Council's work groups into registering engineers, recognising engineering education and enforcing professional conduct.
plainText: NEC roles = registration + recognition of education + conduct and discipline

title: XOR definition
description: Exclusive-OR in sum-of-products form; output is 1 when the inputs differ.

title: XNOR definition
description: Exclusive-NOR (equivalence) is 1 when both inputs are equal; it is the 1-bit comparator.

title: NOT from a universal gate
description: Tying both inputs of a NAND or NOR together gives an inverter; this is the starting point of every NAND-only or NOR-only design.
plainText: NAND(A,A) = NOT A; NOR(A,A) = NOT A

title: Truth table size
description: A gate or function with n inputs has 2^n input combinations, so 3 inputs need 8 rows and 4 inputs need 16.

title: De Morgan's theorems
description: Convert between AND and OR forms under complement; generalises to any number of variables.
plainText: NOT(A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B; NOT(A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B

title: Absorption law
description: A term that contains another term as a factor is absorbed by it.
latex: A + AB = A, \qquad A(A + B) = A
plainText: A + AB = A; A(A + B) = A

title: Redundancy (simplification) theorem
description: The complemented variable in the second term is redundant; the dual form is A(A' + B) = AB.

title: Consensus theorem
description: The consensus term BC, formed from the two terms that contain A and A', is redundant and can be dropped.

title: Distributive law (OR over AND)
description: Unlike ordinary algebra, OR distributes over AND in Boolean algebra; used to expand SOP into POS.

title: Minterm and maxterm relation
description: The maxterm with index i is the complement of the minterm with the same index; each singles out row i of the truth table.

title: Number of minterms
description: A function of n variables has 2^n possible minterms, one per truth-table row; a canonical SOP uses the subset where F = 1.

title: Minterm list to maxterm list
description: The POS maxterm list contains exactly the indices missing from the SOP minterm list, so conversion is immediate.
plainText: F = sum m(S) = product M(all indices not in S)

title: AND-OR to NAND-NAND
description: Double inversion between the two levels turns every AND-OR (SOP) circuit into an all-NAND circuit with identical wiring; OR-AND becomes NOR-NOR the same way.

title: K-map size
description: One cell per minterm; a 4-variable map is 4 x 4 and a 3-variable map is 2 x 4.

title: Variables eliminated by a group
description: A pair removes one variable, a group of 4 removes two, a group of 8 removes three; valid group sizes are powers of 2 only.
plainText: Group of 2^k cells eliminates k variables, leaving n - k literals

title: Adjacency count
description: In an n-variable map each cell differs in one variable from exactly n others, which is why the edges and corners wrap around.
plainText: each cell has n adjacent cells (with wrap-around)

title: POS from the zeros
description: Each group of 0s becomes a sum term in which every constant variable is written complemented; the AND of those terms is the minimal POS.
plainText: Group the 0s to get F' in SOP, then complement with De Morgan to get F in POS

title: 4:1 MUX output
description: Each data input is ANDed with the minterm of the select code that picks it; the products are ORed.

title: Select lines of a MUX
description: A multiplexer with N = 2^n data inputs needs n select lines; a DEMUX with N outputs needs the same.

title: MUX tree size
description: Number of 2^k:1 multiplexers needed to build a 2^n:1 multiplexer when the division is exact (16:1 from 4:1 = 5).

title: DEMUX output
description: Output i of a demultiplexer equals the data input ANDed with the i-th minterm of the select lines; identical to a decoder with enable = D.

title: Decoder output
description: Output i of an n-to-2^n decoder is the i-th minterm of the inputs, active only when enable is asserted.

title: Decoder and encoder sizes
description: A decoder expands a code into one-of-2^n lines; an encoder compresses one-of-2^n lines back into an n-bit code.
plainText: decoder: n to 2^n; encoder: 2^n to n

title: Full adder from a decoder
description: With A, B, C_in on a 3-to-8 decoder, two OR gates on the listed outputs give the sum and carry.
plainText: S = m1 + m2 + m4 + m7; Cout = m3 + m5 + m6 + m7

title: 8-to-3 encoder
description: Each output bit is the OR of the inputs whose index has that bit set; three OR gates form the encoder.

title: Half adder outputs
description: A half adder adds two bits with one XOR gate for the sum and one AND gate for the carry; it has no carry input.
latex: S = A \oplus B, \qquad C = A \cdot B
plainText: S = A XOR B; C = A AND B

title: Full adder outputs
description: Sum and carry of a full adder; the carry can also be written AB + BC_in + AC_in (majority of the three inputs).
latex: S = A \oplus B \oplus C_{in},\quad C_{out} = AB + C_{in}(A \oplus B)
plainText: S = A XOR B XOR Cin; Cout = AB + Cin(A XOR B)

title: Full subtractor outputs
description: Difference is the same XOR as the adder sum; borrow-out is the carry expression with A complemented.
latex: D = A \oplus B \oplus B_{in},\quad B_{out} = \overline{A}B + \overline{A}B_{in} + BB_{in}
plainText: D = A XOR B XOR Bin; Bout = A'B + A'Bin + B Bin

title: Ripple-carry delay
description: Worst-case time for the final carry of an n-stage ripple-carry adder; carry lookahead makes it independent of n.

title: BCD correction
description: After binary addition of two BCD digits, add 6 whenever the sum exceeds 9 or a carry K was produced.

title: Unsigned range
description: An n-bit unsigned number spans 0 to 2^n − 1; a carry-out of 1 from the MSB means the true sum exceeds this range.

title: 2's complement
description: Negative number representation in binary; the same operation negates a negative number back to positive.
plainText: 2's complement = invert all bits, then add 1

title: 2's complement range
description: An n-bit 2's complement number spans one more negative value than positive; for 8 bits, −128 to +127.

title: Value of a 2's complement pattern
description: The sign bit carries a negative weight; all other bits carry their normal positive weights.

title: Overflow detection
description: Signed overflow occurs when the carry into the sign bit differs from the carry out of it.

title: Subtraction by addition
description: Subtraction is performed by adding the 2's complement of the subtrahend and discarding the final carry.

title: Race-around condition
description: A level-triggered JK with J = K = 1 toggles repeatedly while the clock stays HIGH whenever the propagation delay is shorter than the clock pulse width.

title: SR to JK conversion
description: Feeding back the outputs into S and R turns an SR flip-flop into a JK flip-flop and makes J = K = 1 a toggle.

title: JK to D conversion
description: With K the complement of J the JK flip-flop only ever sets or resets, so Q+ = D.

title: D to T conversion
description: An XOR of T with the present output turns a D flip-flop into a toggle flip-flop; T to D is the same relation, T = D xor Q.

title: Shift register delay
description: An n-stage SISO register delays a serial bit stream by n clock periods.

title: Ring and Johnson counter states
description: With n flip-flops a ring counter cycles through n states and a twisted-ring (Johnson) counter through 2n states.
plainText: Ring counter: n states; Johnson counter: 2n states

title: Multiplication and division by shifting
description: Each left shift doubles an unsigned binary number and each right shift halves it, provided no significant bit is shifted out.
plainText: Shift left k places = N × 2^k; shift right k places = floor(N / 2^k)

title: Register capacity
description: A register of n flip-flops holds an n-bit word; a 4-bit register stores 4 bits, one of 16 values.
plainText: n flip-flops store n bits (2^n distinct values)

title: Counter modulus
description: The maximum number of states of an n flip-flop binary counter.
plainText: n flip-flops -> MOD 2^n binary counter; states 0 to 2^n - 1

title: Flip-flops for a MOD-N counter
description: A MOD-N counter needs the smallest n such that 2^n is at least N; the extra states are skipped by reset logic.

title: Frequency division
description: A MOD-N counter divides its clock frequency by N; n binary stages divide it by 2^n.

title: Ripple counter maximum frequency
description: The clock period of an n-stage ripple counter must cover n propagation delays plus any decoder delay.

title: Synchronous up-counter toggle inputs
description: In a synchronous binary up counter a stage toggles only when all lower-order bits are 1.

title: 8085 address space
description: Sixteen address lines A0–A15 give the 8085 a 64 KB memory map from 0000H to FFFFH.

title: RST vector address
description: Restart instruction RST n and hardware pins RST 5.5/6.5/7.5 branch to n × 8: e.g. 6.5 × 8 = 52 = 0034H.

title: 8085 internal clock
description: The on-chip clock generator halves the crystal frequency; a 6.144 MHz crystal gives a 3.072 MHz operating clock.

title: Stack pointer after PUSH/POP
description: Each PUSH stores a register pair (two bytes) and moves the 16-bit stack pointer down; POP reverses it.
plainText: PUSH: SP = SP − 2; POP: SP = SP + 2

title: 8086 memory capacity
description: Twenty address lines A0–A19 give the 8086 a 1 MB physical address space from 00000H to FFFFFH.

title: Bus cycle time
description: Each 8086 bus cycle (T1–T4) takes four clock periods without wait states: 800 ns at 5 MHz.

title: Reset address
description: After reset CS = FFFFH and IP = 0000H, so execution starts 16 bytes below the top of the 1 MB map.

title: 8086 physical address
description: The 20-bit physical address from a 16-bit segment register and a 16-bit offset; e.g. 1234H:0022H → 12362H.

title: Segment size
description: The largest range a 16-bit offset can cover; a segment may be smaller but never larger.

title: Offset from physical address
description: Reverse calculation for a chosen segment value; the result must lie between 0000H and FFFFH.

title: Number of possible segment bases
description: Segments start on 16-byte paragraph boundaries, so there are 65536 possible segment starting addresses in 1 MB.

title: 8086 effective address
description: General form for memory operands; base is BX or BP, index is SI or DI, and each term is optional.

title: Physical address of a data operand
description: Combine the effective address with the default segment to get the 20-bit address the BIU drives onto the bus.
plainText: PA = DS × 10H + EA (SS instead of DS when BP is used)

title: 8085 instruction length
description: Register and indirect instructions are 1 byte, 8-bit immediate or port instructions 2 bytes, 16-bit address or data instructions 3 bytes.
plainText: L = 1 + number of operand bytes (0, 1 or 2)

title: LOOP equivalence
description: LOOP decrements CX and branches while it is non-zero, so a loop set up with MOV CX, n runs n times.
plainText: LOOP L = DEC CX ; JNZ L

title: Stack pointer on PUSH and POP
description: Each stack operation moves a 16-bit word, so SP changes by 2; the stack grows toward lower addresses.

title: MUL result registers
description: Unsigned multiply always uses the accumulator as the implied operand and doubles the width of the result.
latex: AX = AL \times r8,\qquad DX{:}AX = AX \times r16
plainText: MUL r8: AX = AL × r8; MUL r16: DX:AX = AX × r16

title: DIV result registers
description: Unsigned divide of the double-width accumulator; a quotient that does not fit causes a type-0 (divide error) interrupt.
latex: AL = \lfloor AX / r8 \rfloor,\ AH = AX \bmod r8
plainText: DIV r8: AL = quotient, AH = remainder (DIV r16: AX quotient, DX remainder)

title: 8255 I/O line count
description: The 8255 provides 24 programmable I/O lines as Ports A, B and C; Port C can be split into two 4-bit halves.

title: Mode-0 control word
description: Builds any mode-0 control word by adding the input-direction weights to 80H; each flag is 1 for input and 0 for output.
plainText: CW = 80H + 10H (A in) + 08H (C upper in) + 02H (B in) + 01H (C lower in); flags are 1 for input

title: BSR control word
description: With D7 = 0 the control word sets (S = 1) or resets (S = 0) the Port C bit whose number is in D3 D2 D1.
plainText: BSR word = 2 x bit number + S (S = 1 set, S = 0 reset), D7 = 0

title: 8255 register addresses
description: A1 A0 select the four internal registers, so a decoded base address gives four consecutive port addresses on the 8085 (consecutive even addresses on the 8086).
plainText: Port A = base, Port B = base + 1, Port C = base + 2, control = base + 3

title: Bit time
description: Duration of one bit on the line; a UART receiver samples each bit at the middle of this interval.

title: Asynchronous frame length
description: Total bits transmitted per character including the start bit, data bits, optional parity bit and stop bits.

title: Character throughput
description: Number of characters delivered per second on a two-level asynchronous link.
plainText: Characters per second = baud rate / frame bits (9600 baud, 8N1 -> 960)

title: Bit rate from baud rate
description: Each symbol carries log2(M) bits; for binary signalling (M = 2) the bit rate equals the baud rate.
plainText: Bit rate = baud x log2(M), M = signal levels per symbol

title: Link efficiency
description: Fraction of transmitted bits that carry user data; the rest is start, parity and stop overhead.
plainText: Efficiency = data bits / frame bits x 100 % (8N1 -> 80 %)

title: Burst DMA transfer time
description: Time to move N bytes when the DMAC performs one transfer per bus cycle in burst mode.

title: Interrupt-driven CPU cost
description: CPU time consumed to move N bytes through an interrupt service routine; compare with the DMA time to see the saving.
plainText: T_INT = N x t_ISR (time per interrupt service)

title: 8237 maximum block size
description: The 16-bit address and word count registers of each 8237 channel limit a single programmed transfer to 64 KB.
plainText: Block max = 2^16 = 65536 bytes per channel program

title: Maximum DMA data rate
description: Upper bound on DMA throughput set by the bus cycle time of the controller and memory.
plainText: R_DMA = 1 / t_cycle (bytes per second for byte-wide transfers)

title: IVT vector address
description: Physical address of the 4-byte entry for interrupt type n in the 8086 interrupt vector table, which spans 00000H to 003FFH.

title: IVT entry layout
description: Each entry stores the ISR offset in the low word and its segment in the high word; the 8086 loads both to reach the ISR.
plainText: IP from address 4n, CS from address 4n + 2

title: IVT size
description: Total size of the interrupt vector table: 256 types, 4 bytes each.

title: Stack used per 8086 interrupt
description: Three words are pushed when an interrupt is accepted, so nesting k levels needs at least 6k bytes plus whatever each ISR pushes.

title: 8259 cascade capacity
description: Each of the master 8259 IR inputs can be fed by a slave 8259 with 8 inputs, giving 64 sources from nine controllers.

title: De Morgan's theorems
description: Break the bar, change the operator; applies to any number of variables.

title: Full adder
description: Three inputs, two outputs; the carry is the majority function.
latex: S = A \oplus B \oplus C_{in},\qquad C_{out} = AB + C_{in}(A \oplus B)
plainText: Sum = A XOR B XOR C_in;  Carry = AB + C_in(A XOR B)

title: MOD-N counter
description: N is the modulus (number of states); f_in the clock frequency.
plainText: Flip-flops n = ceil(log₂N);  f_out = f_in / N

title: 8086 physical address
description: 20-bit result; the segment is shifted left one hex digit before adding the 16-bit offset.

title: Interrupt vectors
description: n is the interrupt type (8086) or the RST number 0–7 (8085).
plainText: 8086 INT n vector at 4n;  8085 RST n vector at 8n

title: Positional value of a number
description: Value of a base-b number: each digit multiplied by b raised to its position (negative positions for fractional digits) and summed.

title: Range of n unsigned bits
description: An n-bit unsigned binary number can represent 2^n values; 8 bits cover 0 to 255 and 16 bits 0 to 65535.

title: Binary to Gray conversion
description: Keep the most significant bit and XOR each adjacent pair of binary bits to get the remaining Gray bits; 1000 binary becomes 1100 Gray.
plainText: g_MSB = b_MSB; g_i = b_(i+1) XOR b_i

title: Noise margins
description: Noise a signal can tolerate before an input misreads it; standard TTL gives 0.4 V on both sides, 5 V CMOS gives about 0.9 V and 1.17 V.
latex: NM_H = V_{OH(min)} - V_{IH(min)}, \quad NM_L = V_{IL(max)} - V_{OL(max)}
plainText: NM_H = V_OH(min) - V_IH(min); NM_L = V_IL(max) - V_OL(max)

title: Combinational output
description: Each output of a combinational circuit is a Boolean function of the present inputs alone, with no state term.

title: Truth table size
description: A circuit with n inputs has a truth table of 2^n rows, one for every input combination.

title: Number of Boolean functions
description: There are 2^(2^n) distinct Boolean functions of n variables: 16 for two variables, 256 for three.

title: JK characteristic equation
description: Next state of a JK flip-flop; J = K = 1 makes Q+ = Q-bar (toggle).

title: T characteristic equation
description: A T flip-flop toggles when T = 1 and holds when T = 0.

title: SR characteristic equation
description: Next state of an SR latch or flip-flop; the constraint SR = 0 excludes the invalid input pair.

title: D characteristic equation
description: The D flip-flop stores the value of D present at the active clock edge.

title: Maximum clock frequency
description: The clock period must cover the flip-flop propagation delay, the setup time and the delay of logic between flip-flops.

title: Addressable locations
description: The number of memory locations a processor can select directly; 8085 (n = 16) gives 64 KB, 8086 (n = 20) gives 1 MB.
plainText: N = 2^n locations for n address lines

title: T-state duration
description: One T-state is one clock period; at 3 MHz it is 333 ns, at 5 MHz it is 200 ns.

title: Instruction time
description: Multiply the T-state count of an instruction (4 to 18 on the 8085) by the clock period to get its execution time.
plainText: Instruction time = total T-states × T-state duration

title: MIPS rating
description: Millions of instructions per second from the clock frequency and the average number of clocks per instruction.

title: Address lines vs memory size
description: The width of the address bus fixes the number of addressable locations; each extra line doubles the space.

title: Chip capacity
description: A chip described as 'locations x width' stores that many bits; divide by 8 for bytes and take log2 of the locations for the address lines.
plainText: Capacity = locations x width (e.g. 2K x 8 = 16384 bits = 2 KB)

title: Number of chips
description: Tells both how many identical chips build a memory and how many high-order address lines the decoder must consume (log2 of the chip count).
plainText: Chips = total memory / chip size; log2(chips) = decoder lines needed

title: 8085 isolated I/O ports
description: In I/O-mapped I/O on the 8085 the port address is one byte, giving 256 input and 256 output addresses independent of the 64 KB memory map.
plainText: 8085 IN/OUT use an 8-bit port address -> 256 ports

title: 8085 RST n vector
description: The eight 8085 software restart instructions jump to fixed addresses 8 bytes apart, from RST 0 at 0000H to RST 7 at 0038H.

title: 8085 hardware vectors
description: Vector addresses of the four vectored 8085 interrupts; each fractional RST vector lies midway between two integer RST vectors.

title: 8086 type-to-vector address
description: The 8086 finds the ISR for interrupt type n at memory address 4n in the interrupt vector table (NMI is type 2, so 00008H).

title: Interrupt latency
description: Delay between an interrupt request and the first ISR instruction; worst case includes the longest instruction and any interval during which interrupts are disabled.
plainText: Latency = finish current instruction + save state + fetch vector

title: Shift operators
description: Left shift by n multiplies by 2^n and right shift divides by 2^n, so 1 << 3 = 8 and 16 >> 2 = 4.
latex: x \ll n = x \times 2^{n},\qquad x \gg n = \lfloor x / 2^{n} \rfloor
plainText: x << n = x * 2^n; x >> n = x / 2^n (non-negative integers)

title: Division and modulus identity
description: Integer division truncates toward zero and the remainder takes the sign of the dividend: -7 / 2 = -3 and -7 % 2 = -1.
plainText: (a / b) * b + a % b == a; sign of a % b follows a

title: Ternary operator
description: Compact conditional expression; only the selected branch is evaluated, and it can be nested to mimic an else-if ladder.

title: Bitwise complement
description: Flipping every bit of a signed integer gives its negative minus one: ~0 = -1, ~5 = -6, ~(-1) = 0.

title: Format specifier syntax
description: Flags (-, +, 0, space, #), a minimum field width, a precision after the dot, a length modifier (l, ll, h) and finally the conversion letter (d i u f e g c s x o p).

title: fgets bound
description: The size argument makes fgets safe where gets is not; the newline is kept if it fits, so strip it with s[strcspn(s, "\n")] = 0 if needed.
plainText: fgets(s, n, stdin) stores at most n - 1 characters plus '\0'

title: Return values of printf and scanf
description: printf("%d", printf("hi")) prints hi2, and checking scanf's return is the only way to detect bad input.
plainText: printf returns characters written; scanf returns items converted (or EOF)

title: Default precision of %f
description: printf("%f", 3.14) prints 3.140000, printf("%.2f", 3.14159) prints 3.14 and printf("%.0f", 2.5) prints 2 (round-half-even in glibc).

title: Iterations of a counted for loop
description: With <= the count is floor((b - a)/s) + 1; for step 1 this is b - a versus b - a + 1, the source of every off-by-one question.
plainText: for (i = a; i < b; i += s) runs ceil((b - a)/s) times

title: Doubling loop
description: A counter that doubles (or halves) each time runs a logarithmic number of times: n = 100 gives 7 iterations, n = 1024 gives 10.
plainText: for (i = 1; i < n; i *= 2) runs ceil(log2 n) times

title: Nested loop counts
description: The inner body runs once for every combination of outer and inner values; a triangular inner bound gives the sum 0 + 1 + ... + (n - 1).
plainText: independent nested loops: n * m; triangular (j < i): n(n - 1)/2

title: for loop syntax
description: init runs once, condition is checked BEFORE each iteration, update runs after the body; all three parts are optional and for (;;) loops forever.

title: Factorial recursion
description: The textbook recursive definition: fact(4) = 4 * fact(3) = 24, and a recursive fact(n) makes n calls with stack depth n.

title: Fibonacci recursion
description: Two base cases and two recursive calls per step give the sequence 0 1 1 2 3 5 8 13; the naive version costs about 2^n calls.

title: Euclid's GCD
description: Each step replaces the pair by (b, a mod b) until the remainder is 0: gcd(48, 18) -> gcd(18, 12) -> gcd(12, 6) -> gcd(6, 0) = 6.
plainText: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b); gcd(a, 0) = a

title: Function prototype
description: Declares a function before use so the compiler can check the call; parameter names are optional in a prototype and the line ends with a semicolon.

title: Array size in bytes
description: int a[5] occupies 5 * 4 = 20 bytes, double d[10] occupies 80 bytes; dividing by the size of one element recovers the element count.
plainText: sizeof(a) = n * sizeof(type); n = sizeof(a) / sizeof(a[0])

title: Address of a 1-D element
description: For int a[5] starting at 1000, a[3] lives at 1000 + 3 * 4 = 1012; the same rule underlies a[i] == *(a + i).

title: Row-major address in a 2-D array
description: C stores rows one after another, so for int m[3][4] at 2000, &m[2][1] = 2000 + (2 * 4 + 1) * 4 = 2036.

title: String storage
description: A string of n characters needs n + 1 bytes for the terminating null; sizeof counts it, strlen does not.

title: Subscript identity
description: Array subscripting is defined through pointer arithmetic, so an array name and a pointer to its first element can be indexed identically.

title: 2-D element address
description: Row-major storage lets any element of a 2-D array be reached from the first element by a linear offset.

title: Element count of an array
description: Valid only where arr is declared as an array; on a function parameter it gives the pointer size divided by the element size.

title: Function pointer declaration
description: The parentheses around *fp are essential; int *fp(int, int) would declare a function returning int *.
plainText: int (*fp)(int, int) = add; call as fp(2, 3)

title: Structure size
description: Padding for alignment can make the structure larger than the plain sum; struct { char c; int i; } is typically 8 bytes.

title: Union size
description: All members overlap in one block, so the block only needs to be as large as the biggest member (rounded to its alignment).

title: Alignment rule
description: Explains where padding bytes go: a 4-byte int after a 1-byte char is placed at offset 4, leaving 3 padding bytes.
plainText: each member starts at an offset that is a multiple of its alignment

title: Enumeration values
description: enum { A, B = 4, C } gives A = 0, B = 4, C = 5.
plainText: enum constants count from 0 and each is previous + 1 unless given a value

title: Array of structures size
description: Total memory of a table of records, with the per-record size including any padding.

title: Arrow operator identity
description: Both forms read member m through a pointer; the arrow is shorthand and the parentheses in the long form are mandatory.

title: Record i through a pointer
description: A structure pointer advances one whole record per step, so array indexing and pointer arithmetic give the same member.

title: Heap table of records
description: Allocates n records at run time; access as t[i].m or (t + i)->m and release with free(t).

title: Record offset
description: Used with fseek(fp, offset, SEEK_SET) to jump straight to the n-th fixed-length record in a binary file.
plainText: offset of record n = n × sizeof(record), n from 0

title: File size
description: Moving to the end and reading the position indicator gives the number of bytes in the file.

title: Record count
description: The number of fixed-length records stored in a binary file.

title: Origin constants
description: The third argument of fseek chooses the reference point; EOF is the value the character and formatted input functions return at end of file.

title: Object size
description: Only non-static data members occupy space in each object; member functions, static members and access specifiers add nothing.
plainText: sizeof(object) = sum of non-static data members + padding

title: Empty class size
description: Guarantees every object has a unique address; a common numeric MCQ.
plainText: sizeof of a class with no data members is 1 byte

title: Member access syntax
description: Dot for an object or reference, arrow for a pointer; both have higher precedence than unary *.
plainText: obj.m for objects; p->m, equivalent to (*p).m, for pointers

title: Constructor family
description: Default, parameterised and copy constructors plus the single destructor; all share the class name and none has a return type.

title: Dynamic array of objects
description: Allocates n × sizeof(T) bytes, runs the default constructor n times, and delete[] runs n destructors in reverse order.

title: Destruction order
description: Last constructed, first destroyed, for local objects in a scope and for elements of an array.
plainText: Objects are destroyed in the reverse order of construction

title: Static member definition
description: Declaration inside, single definition outside without the static keyword; one copy shared by all objects.
plainText: static int c; inside the class; int Cls::c = 0; outside the class, exactly once

title: Type of this
description: The pointer itself cannot be reseated; in a const member function the pointed-to object is also const.
plainText: this is a constant pointer to the current object (const Class* const inside a const member function)

title: Chaining via *this
description: Each call returns a reference to the same object, so the next call operates on it too.
plainText: A member function that returns *this by reference allows a.f().g().h()

title: Friend function call form
description: A friend is a non-member: it receives the object as an argument and has no this pointer.
plainText: friend R f(const Cls &); is called as f(obj), never obj.f()

title: Promotion and truncation
description: In a mixed expression the smaller type is promoted to the larger; converting a floating value to int truncates toward zero.

title: Basic and class conversions
description: A one-argument constructor converts a basic value into an object; a conversion function converts an object into a basic value.
plainText: basic -> class: constructor T(basic); class -> basic: operator basic()

title: Class to class conversion
description: Write the conversion in exactly one of the two classes; defining both makes the conversion ambiguous.
plainText: Dest(const Src&) in the destination, or operator Dest() in the source

title: One user-defined conversion
description: The compiler chains standard conversions freely but applies at most one constructor or conversion function implicitly.
plainText: At most one user-defined conversion per implicit conversion sequence

title: Inheritance syntax
description: One base gives single inheritance; a comma-separated list gives multiple inheritance; the mode defaults to private for class and public for struct.
latex: \text{class D : mode B1, mode B2 \{ \};}\quad \text{mode = public | protected | private}
plainText: class Derived : access-mode Base1, access-mode Base2 { };

title: Constructor and destructor order
description: Construction is top-down and destruction is bottom-up, in single and multilevel inheritance alike.
plainText: Constructors: Base then Derived; destructors: Derived then Base

title: Diamond sub-object count
description: Virtual inheritance in the intermediate classes collapses the duplicated base into one shared sub-object.
plainText: Diamond: 2 copies of the top base without virtual, 1 copy with virtual base class

title: Calls in a multilevel chain
description: Every level of a multilevel hierarchy contributes exactly one constructor and one destructor call for each object created.
latex: n\text{-level chain} \Rightarrow n \text{ ctor calls},\ n \text{ dtor calls}
plainText: n classes in a chain: n constructor calls and n destructor calls per object

title: Field width
description: width(n)/setw(n) pads the next item with the fill character up to n columns but never cuts a longer value; it resets to 0 after one use.

title: Precision meaning
description: setprecision(3) prints 3.14159 as 3.14 by default but as 3.142 after fixed, and 1234.5 becomes 1.23e+03 in general notation.
plainText: general notation: p significant digits; fixed/scientific: p digits after the point

title: Two-argument setf
description: setf(ios::hex, ios::basefield) first clears dec/hex/oct then sets hex; the one-argument setf(ios::hex) would leave dec set as well.
plainText: flags = (flags AND NOT field) OR flag

title: Stream defaults
description: The state every stream starts with; cout << 3.14159265 therefore prints 3.14159 (6 significant digits) with no padding.
plainText: width 0, precision 6, fill space, flags skipws | dec

title: Record offset
description: Byte position passed to seekg/seekp to reach the n-th fixed-size record counted from 1.

title: Record count
description: Seek to ios::end, read tellg() to get the file size in bytes and divide by the record size.

title: Default open modes
description: What each class opens with when no mode is given; ios::out alone also truncates the file.
plainText: ifstream -> ios::in, ofstream -> ios::out, fstream -> ios::in | ios::out

title: Random access call
description: Moves the get pointer; seekp does the same for the put pointer, and tellg/tellp report the current offsets.

title: vector access cost
description: A vector is a contiguous dynamic array, so indexing is constant time and appending is constant on average because capacity doubles when it runs out.
plainText: v[i] is O(1); push_back is O(1) amortised

title: Associative container cost
description: Ordered associative containers are balanced binary search trees; unordered ones are hash tables with no element ordering.
plainText: set/map operations O(log n); unordered_set/map O(1) average

title: Algorithm complexity
description: The three algorithm costs most often asked; binary_search is only valid when the range is already sorted.
plainText: sort O(n log n); find O(n); binary_search O(log n) on a sorted range

title: Half-open range
description: Every STL range excludes end(), which points one past the last element; an empty container has begin() == end().

title: Handler search
description: Handlers of a try block are tested top to bottom and the first whose type matches (exactly or by derived-to-base conversion) runs; the rest are skipped.
plainText: throw → stack unwinding → first matching catch in written order

title: Uncaught exception
description: When the search leaves main() without a match, terminate() is called; set_terminate() can replace the default handler but the program still cannot resume.

title: Exception specifications
description: Both declare a non-throwing function; the old dynamic specifications throw(T1, T2) that called unexpected() on violation were deprecated in C++11 and removed in C++17.

title: Integer ranges
description: n is the number of bits: 8 for char, 16 for short, 32 for int on typical compilers.

title: Array size and 2-D address
description: Row-major storage: all of row 0, then row 1, and so on.
plainText: size = n × sizeof(type);  &a[i][j] = base + (i × cols + j) × sizeof(type)

title: Pointer arithmetic
description: Adding i moves i elements; subtracting two pointers gives an element count.
plainText: p + i = address of p + i × sizeof(*p)

title: struct and union sizes
description: Padding aligns members, so a struct can be larger than the plain sum.
plainText: union: largest member;  struct: sum of members plus any padding

title: Range of int
description: A 4-byte signed int in two's complement covers -2^31 to 2^31 - 1; unsigned int covers 0 to 2^32 - 1 = 4,294,967,295.

title: Range of an n-bit type
description: Works for every integer width: char (n = 8) gives -128 to 127 or 0 to 255, short (n = 16) gives -32,768 to 32,767 or 0 to 65,535.

title: Size ordering guarantee
description: The only sizes the standard fixes are the ordering and sizeof(char) = 1; the typical values are char 1, short 2, int 4, long 4 or 8, long long 8, float 4, double 8.
plainText: sizeof(char) = 1 <= sizeof(short) <= sizeof(int) <= sizeof(long) <= sizeof(long long)

title: Character arithmetic
description: A char is a small integer holding an ASCII code, so characters can be added, compared and converted with plain arithmetic.

title: Pointer increment
