description: Pointer arithmetic is scaled by the size of the pointed-to type, so p + 1 on an int pointer adds 4 bytes and on a double pointer adds 8.
plainText: p + i → address of p + i × sizeof(*p)

title: Pointer difference
description: Subtracting two pointers into the same array gives the number of elements between them, not the number of bytes.

title: Pointer size
description: All object pointers have the same size, fixed by the address width of the machine, whatever type they point to.

title: Heap allocation size
description: The standard way to request space for n objects of type T; calloc additionally zeroes the block.

title: Overload resolution order
description: The ranking the compiler uses to choose among overloaded functions; a tie between two candidates makes the call ambiguous.
plainText: exact match > promotion > standard conversion > user-defined conversion

title: Argument counts with defaults
description: A function whose k rightmost parameters have default values can be called with any count from n - k up to n arguments.
plainText: n - k <= number of arguments <= n, for n parameters with k trailing defaults

title: Scope resolution
description: The three everyday uses of the :: operator, which has the highest precedence in C++.
plainText: ns::name (namespace member), ::global (hidden global), Class::member (define member outside class)

title: Macro expansion trap
description: Textual macro substitution ignores precedence; an inline function evaluates its argument once and correctly.
plainText: #define SQR(x) x * x makes SQR(a+b) expand to a + b * a + b, not (a+b)^2

title: Operator call rewriting
description: The compiler translates an operator expression into a call of the overloaded operator function.
plainText: a + b is a.operator+(b) (member) or operator+(a, b) (non-member)

title: Parameter count
description: A member operator gets its left operand as *this, so unary members take 0 parameters and binary members take 1; friends take 1 and 2.
plainText: member: n - 1 parameters, friend: n parameters (n = number of operands)

title: Prefix vs postfix increment
description: The dummy int parameter distinguishes postfix from prefix; postfix returns the old value by value.
plainText: prefix: T& operator++()  |  postfix: T operator++(int)

title: Non-overloadable operators
description: These five operators (plus typeid and the cast operators) keep their built-in meaning; all others can be overloaded.

title: Pure virtual declaration
description: Appending = 0 makes the function pure virtual and the enclosing class abstract; derived classes must override it to be instantiable.

title: Object size with vptr
description: A class with any virtual function carries one hidden pointer, so a class holding a single int plus a virtual function is 8 bytes on a 32-bit build and 16 bytes on a 64-bit build after alignment.

title: Virtual call resolution
description: A virtual call reads the object's vptr, indexes the class vtable and jumps to the stored address: constant time, one indirection more than a direct call.

title: Template instantiation
description: The compiler generates one concrete function or class per distinct set of template arguments; an unused template produces no code at all.
plainText: instantiations = number of distinct <T> argument sets used

title: Stack<T, N> storage
description: A class template with a non-type parameter N holding T data[N] needs N × sizeof(T) bytes for its array, e.g. Stack<double, 5> needs 40 bytes plus the top index.
plainText: storage of T data[N] = N × sizeof(T) bytes

title: Overload preference
description: The order in which overload resolution ranks candidates when a call could go to an ordinary function or to a function template.
plainText: non-template exact match > template exact match > match needing a conversion

title: CAR width
description: The control address register and the AD field need n bits for a control memory of 2^n words; 128 words need 7 bits.

title: Microinstruction length
description: Mano's microinstruction is 20 bits: three 3-bit microoperation fields, 2-bit condition, 2-bit branch, 7-bit address.
latex: w = F_1 + F_2 + F_3 + CD + BR + AD

title: Control memory size
description: Total ROM capacity of the control memory; 128 × 20 = 2560 bits.

title: Relative addressing
description: The address field is added to the (already incremented) program counter; used for short, position-independent branches.

title: Indexed and base addressing
description: The address field is added to an index register (array stepping) or a base register (segment relocation).
latex: EA = XR + A \quad\text{or}\quad EA = BR + A
plainText: EA = XR + A (indexed) or EA = BR + A (base register)

title: Indirect addressing
description: The address field points to a memory word that holds the effective address, so the operand costs two memory reads.

title: Arithmetic shift
description: Arithmetic shifts keep the sign bit so they multiply and divide signed numbers by two.

title: CPU time
description: Execution time of a program; RISC lowers CPI and T_clk while CISC lowers IC, and only the product matters.

title: Relative speed at equal clock
description: Ratio of execution times of two instruction sets running at the same clock frequency.

title: Register window total
description: Registers in a file with W overlapped windows, L locals and C common registers per window and G globals; Berkeley RISC I: (10 + 6) × 8 + 10 = 138.

title: Pipeline speedup
description: Speedup of a k-segment pipeline processing n tasks when every segment takes one clock; 4 stages and 100 tasks give 3.88.

title: General speedup
description: Speedup when a non-pipelined task takes t_n and the pipeline clock is t_p; tends to t_n/t_p for large n.

title: Pipeline efficiency
description: Fraction of the ideal speedup k actually obtained; approaches 1 as the number of tasks grows.

title: Pipeline throughput
description: Tasks completed per unit time; the ideal is one task per clock period t_p.

title: Average access time, two levels
description: Effective access time of a two-level hierarchy with hit ratio h in the fast level; the same form gives cache-plus-main-memory or main-memory-plus-disk figures.

title: Disk access time
description: Seek time plus average rotational latency (half a revolution at r rev/s) plus the transfer time of b bytes from a track holding N bytes.

title: Average rotational latency
description: Half of one revolution period; 7200 rpm gives 4.17 ms, 5400 rpm gives 5.56 ms, 15000 rpm gives 2 ms.

title: Hamming check bits
description: Minimum number k of check bits that can locate any single-bit error in m data bits: 8 data bits need 4, 32 need 6, 64 need 7.

title: Average memory access time
description: With hit ratio h, cache time t_c and memory time t_m; for example h = 0.9, t_c = 10 ns, t_m = 100 ns gives 19 ns.

title: Number of lines and sets
description: A cache of C bytes with K-byte blocks has m lines; a k-way set-associative cache groups them into v sets, each indexed by log2 v address bits.
plainText: m = C / K lines; v = m / k sets

title: Tag field width
description: Address bits left after the set (or line) index and the word offset; for a fully associative cache the index term is 0 and the tag is the whole block number.

title: Two-level cache access time
description: Average access time with an L1 and an L2 cache; the L2 term is weighted by the L1 miss ratio.

title: Chips needed for a composed memory
description: Total bits wanted divided by bits per chip; 4K × 16 from 1K × 8 chips needs (4096 × 16)/(1024 × 8) = 8 chips arranged as 4 rows of 2.

title: Address and decoder lines
description: The composed memory needs log2(words) address lines; the highest n_dec of them feed the decoder that selects one row of chips, the rest go to every chip.

title: Sequential-device transfer time
description: Time to read n bits: average access (positioning) time plus the bits divided by the transfer rate; for RAM the same idea gives transfer rate = 1 / cycle time.

title: Wait states
description: Number of idle clock cycles the processor must insert when the memory's access time exceeds what the bus cycle allows; zero when the memory is fast enough.

title: DMA block transfer time
description: Time to move N words in burst mode when each word takes one memory cycle of t_cycle.

title: CPU time under programmed I/O
description: N words, each costing c_word CPU cycles of polling and moving, at clock frequency f_clk.

title: Cycle-stealing slowdown
description: Fraction of CPU bus time lost when one memory cycle is stolen every t_word (the device's word interval).

title: Words in a block
description: Convert a block size to the number of DMA transfers; 4 KB on a 32-bit (4-byte) bus is 1024 transfers.
plainText: N = block bytes / bus width in bytes

title: Amdahl's law
description: Speed-up on N processors when only a fraction f of the work is parallelisable; f = 0.9, N = 10 gives 5.26.

title: Maximum speed-up
description: The ceiling as the number of processors grows without limit; a 10% serial part caps the speed-up at 10.

title: Hypercube parameters
description: For an n-dimensional binary cube; each node has n neighbours differing in one address bit.

title: Omega network size
description: An N×N omega network made of 2×2 interchange switches; 8×8 needs 3 stages and 12 switches.

title: Parallel efficiency
description: Fraction of the ideal N-fold speed-up actually achieved.

title: Test-and-set semantics
description: The old semaphore value is copied into flag F and the semaphore is set to 1 without releasing the bus in between.

title: Fully connected links
description: Number of point-to-point links needed to connect every pair of N nodes directly; 8 nodes need 28 links.

title: Time-slice bus share
description: In time-slice arbitration each of N processors owns the bus for an equal fixed interval per round.

title: Speed-up with synchronization cost
description: Lock, barrier and communication time T_sync added to the ideal T1/N reduces the achievable speed-up.

title: State register width
description: Minimum number of flip-flops in the controller state register for binary encoding; one-hot encoding instead uses N_states flip-flops.

title: Maximum clock frequency
description: The clock period of a datapath or FSM must cover the slowest register-to-register path; separating a slow operation into more states shortens this path.

title: Execution time
description: Merging FSMD states reduces N_cycles while separating states allows a shorter T_clk; the product is what the user experiences.

title: States from n flip-flops
description: An n-bit binary-encoded state register can represent up to 2^n distinct controller states.
plainText: Maximum states = 2^n for an n-bit state register

title: CPU execution time
description: Time to run a program of IC instructions with average CPI cycles per instruction at clock frequency f_clk; a program of 10^6 instructions at CPI 2 on 100 MHz takes 20 ms.

title: MIPS rating
description: Millions of instructions per second; a simple processor-selection metric that is only meaningful between processors with similar instruction sets.

title: Pipeline speedup
description: Ideal speedup of a k-stage pipeline over a non-pipelined processor for n instructions; 100 instructions on 5 stages give 500 / 104 = 4.81, approaching 5 for large n.

title: Memory address space
description: Size of the program or data memory space visible to the programmer; 16 address bits give 64 K locations, 32 bits give 4 G.
plainText: N = 2^n locations for n address bits

title: FIR multiply-accumulate
description: The inner loop of digital filtering; an N-tap filter needs N multiply-accumulate operations per output sample, which is why DSPs have a single-cycle MAC unit.

title: ASIC versus FPGA break-even volume
description: Production volume above which an ASIC with high NRE and low unit cost becomes cheaper than an FPGA; for NRE 300,000 and unit costs 20 and 5 the break-even is 20,000 units.

title: Fixed-point Q format
description: In a fixed-point DSP a Qm.f number has m integer bits and f fraction bits; Q15 (1 sign bit, 15 fraction bits) has resolution 2^-15 and covers -1 to just under +1.

title: Timer overflow period
description: Period of an n-bit free-running MCU timer fed through a prescaler; an 8-bit timer with prescaler 64 at 16 MHz overflows every 1.024 ms.

title: RMS utilisation bound
description: Sufficient test for schedulability of n independent periodic tasks under rate-monotonic scheduling.

title: EDF utilisation test
description: Necessary and sufficient test for pre-emptive EDF when deadlines equal periods.

title: RMS asymptotic bound
description: Any number of tasks with total utilisation at most 69.3% is RMS-schedulable.

title: Average waiting time
description: Common figure of merit used to compare FCFS, SJF, RR and priority schedules.
plainText: Average waiting time = sum of waits / n

title: Semaphore count
description: Resulting counting-semaphore value after a sequence of wait and signal operations when no task remains blocked.

title: Polling overhead
description: Fraction of CPU time consumed by a polling driver, e.g. 10 µs x 1000 polls/s = 1%.
plainText: Overhead = time per poll x polling frequency

title: Closed-loop gain
description: Overall gain of a negative-feedback loop with forward gain G and feedback gain H.

title: PID control law
description: Controller output as the sum of proportional, integral and derivative actions on the error.
latex: u(t) = K_p e + K_i \int e\,dt + K_d \frac{de}{dt}
plainText: u = Kp e + Ki integral(e) dt + Kd de/dt

title: Step steady-state error
description: Residual error of a unity-feedback type-0 system to a unit step, where K_pos is the loop DC gain.

title: Discrete PID
description: Sampled form of PID executed once per sampling period T in a microcontroller.
latex: u[k] = K_p e[k] + K_i T \sum e[j] + K_d \frac{e[k] - e[k-1]}{T}
plainText: u[k] = Kp e[k] + Ki T sum e + Kd (e[k]-e[k-1])/T

title: Signed range
description: Range of an n-bit 2's complement (signed) value.

title: Overflow flag
description: Signed overflow is the XOR of the carries into and out of the sign bit.

title: Wraparound sum
description: An n-bit adder keeps only the low n bits of the true sum.

title: Fixed-point value
description: Value of a Qm.f number whose stored integer reading is N.

title: FSM flip-flops (binary)
description: Minimum flip-flops to encode N states in binary; one-hot needs N.

title: Counter divider output
description: Frequency of the MSB of an n-bit free-running counter.

title: Counter modulus
description: Number of distinct states of an n-bit binary counter before it wraps.

title: Pipeline speedup
description: Speedup of a k-stage pipeline over a non-pipelined unit for n items with equal stage times.

title: Maximum clock frequency
description: Highest clock rate allowed by the critical register-to-register path.

title: Dynamic CMOS power
description: Switching power depends on activity, capacitance, supply voltage squared and frequency.

title: LUT size
description: Configuration bits needed by a k-input FPGA look-up table.

title: Pipeline speedup
description: k stages, n tasks; equal stage times assumed; tends to k for large n.

title: Cache average access time
description: h is the hit ratio, t_c the cache time, t_m the main-memory time (add t_c if the miss also pays the cache lookup).

title: Amdahl's law
description: f is the parallelisable fraction, N the number of processors; the serial part caps the speedup.

title: Rate-monotonic bound
description: C_i execution time, T_i period; sufficient condition, tending to 0.693 for many tasks; EDF allows U ≤ 1.

title: Closed-loop transfer function
description: G forward-path gain, H feedback gain; negative feedback reduces the gain but improves accuracy and stability.

title: Full adder cell
description: One-bit sum and carry of the cell that, repeated n times, forms the ALU's parallel adder.
latex: S = A \oplus B \oplus C_{in},\quad C_{out} = AB + C_{in}(A \oplus B)
plainText: S = A XOR B XOR Cin; Cout = AB + Cin(A XOR B)

title: Signed overflow
description: Overflow occurs in 2's complement addition when the carry into the sign bit differs from the carry out of it.

title: Address width
description: The address register needs n bits for 2^n words; Mano's 4096-word memory needs a 12-bit AR and PC.

title: Bus select lines
description: A common bus fed by 8 registers or memory is steered by 3 select lines S2 S1 S0.

title: 2's complement range
description: An n-bit 2's complement register holds one more negative than positive value; 8 bits give −128 to +127, 16 bits give −32768 to +32767.

title: Signed overflow flag
description: Overflow after a 2's complement add or subtract is the XOR of the carry out of the sign bit and the carry into it; equivalently, both operands share a sign that the result does not.

title: IEEE 754 value
description: Value of a normalised single-precision number; for double precision replace 127 by 1023 and use 52 fraction bits.

title: BCD addition correction
description: Correction that turns a binary 4-bit adder into a decimal (BCD) adder by skipping the six invalid codes 1010 to 1111.
plainText: If the 4-bit sum exceeds 9 or produces a carry, add 0110 (6)

title: Addressable I/O ports
description: An 8-bit port address in IN/OUT instructions selects one of 256 input and 256 output ports.

title: Asynchronous frame length
description: A character with 8 data bits, 1 parity and 1 stop bit occupies 11 bit times on the line.
plainText: frame bits = 1 start + d data + p parity + s stop

title: Character rate of a serial line
description: 9600 baud with 11-bit frames delivers about 873 characters per second.
plainText: characters per second = baud / frame bits

title: Line efficiency
description: Fraction of line time carrying useful data; 8/10 = 80% without parity, 8/11 ≈ 73% with parity.

title: Cost per unit
description: Total cost of one product when the one-time NRE cost is amortised over N units; a high-NRE custom design becomes cheaper than a general-purpose one only at large N.
plainText: Cost per unit = unit cost + NRE / N

title: Time-to-market revenue loss
description: Fraction of lifetime revenue lost by entering the market D months late when the market window lasts 2W months (simplified triangular revenue model).

title: Dynamic power
description: Switching power of CMOS logic; lowering supply voltage V has the largest effect, and clock gating reduces the activity factor alpha.
plainText: P_dyn = alpha x C x V^2 x f

title: Moore's law
description: Empirical growth of IC transistor density that lets embedded systems pack more functionality into cheaper, smaller and lower-power chips every generation.
plainText: Transistor count doubles roughly every 18 months

title: Interrupt response time
description: Total time from an interrupt request until its service routine has finished.
plainText: Response time = interrupt latency + ISR execution time

title: Context-switch overhead
description: Fraction of CPU time lost to switching when each time slice q is followed by a switch of length t_cs.

title: Waiting time
description: Time a task spends in the ready queue, where turnaround = completion time - arrival time.
plainText: Waiting time = turnaround time - burst time

title: Vector length
description: Number of elements in a std_logic_vector range, returned by the 'length attribute.
plainText: length of (h downto l) = h - l + 1

title: Unsigned range
description: Values an n-bit unsigned (or std_logic_vector read as unsigned) can hold.

title: Integer range width
description: Width synthesis uses for integer range 0 to M.

title: Switch collision domains
description: Every switch or bridge port that has a device or segment attached is its own collision domain.
plainText: Collision domains = switch ports in use

title: Broadcast domains
description: Without VLANs, only router interfaces split broadcast domains, so each active interface is one broadcast domain.
plainText: Broadcast domains = router interfaces in use

title: Hub collision domain
description: All ports of a hub share one medium, so however many ports it has, it forms a single collision domain.

title: Nyquist bit rate
description: Maximum bit rate of a noiseless channel of bandwidth B hertz using L discrete signal levels.

title: Shannon capacity
description: Theoretical maximum error-free data rate of a noisy channel, with S/N as a plain power ratio.

title: SNR in decibels
description: Converts a signal-to-noise power ratio to decibels; invert with S/N = 10^(dB/10).

title: Transmission delay
description: Time to place all L bits of a frame on a link of rate R bits per second.

title: Propagation delay
description: Time for a signal to travel distance d at propagation speed v through the medium.

title: Stop-and-wait efficiency
description: Fraction of time the link carries data when one frame is sent per round trip; a = t_prop / t_frame.

title: Sliding-window efficiency
description: With W frames outstanding the link is fully used once W ≥ 1 + 2a.

title: ARQ maximum windows
description: Largest sender window for m-bit sequence numbers that avoids ambiguity between old and new frames.

title: Transmission time
description: Time to put an L-bit frame onto a link of bandwidth B bits per second.

title: Pure ALOHA throughput
description: Successful frames per frame time for offered load G; maximum 18.4% at G = 0.5.

title: Slotted ALOHA throughput
description: Successful frames per slot for offered load G; maximum 36.8% at G = 1.

title: CSMA/CD minimum frame
description: Smallest frame that is still being transmitted when a collision from the far end is detected.

title: Binary exponential backoff
description: After the n-th collision a station waits K slot times, with K picked at random from this range.

title: Ethernet frame size limits
description: Destination address through CRC; the data field carries 46 to 1500 bytes.

title: Ethernet slot time
description: Backoff unit and minimum frame duration; 51.2 µs at 10 Mbps and 5.12 µs at 100 Mbps.

title: Ethernet header overhead
description: Addresses, type and CRC added to every payload (26 bytes if the preamble and SFD are counted).

title: MAC address space
description: A 48-bit MAC splits into a 24-bit vendor OUI and a 24-bit interface-specific part.

title: ATM cell efficiency
description: Fraction of each 53-byte ATM cell that carries user payload; the 5-byte header is overhead.

title: PPP frame overhead
description: Bytes PPP adds around each payload with a 16-bit FCS and separate opening and closing flags.
plainText: flag + address + control + protocol + FCS(2) + flag = 8 bytes

title: Bellman-Ford equation
description: Distance vector update: the best cost from x to y is the minimum over neighbours v of the link cost to v plus v's advertised cost to y.

title: Dijkstra relaxation
description: After node w is made permanent, each neighbour v's tentative distance is lowered if the path through w is shorter.

title: Dijkstra complexity
description: Running time of the link state route computation for N nodes and E links.
plainText: O(N^2) with an array, O(E log N) with a heap

title: OSPF interface cost
description: Default OSPF metric with a 100 Mbps reference bandwidth: 10 Mbps gives 10, 100 Mbps gives 1.

title: Path metric
description: RIP adds 1 per hop and OSPF adds interface costs; the path with the smallest total is installed.
plainText: C_path = sum of c_i over the links

title: RIP infinity
description: A RIP route with metric 16 is unreachable, which limits RIP networks to a 15-hop diameter.

title: IPv4 header length
description: HLEN counts 4-byte words, so 5 means a 20-byte header and 15 means the maximum 60 bytes.

title: Fragment offset
description: The 13-bit offset field is measured in 8-byte units, so a fragment starting at data byte 2960 has offset 370.

title: Data per fragment
description: The largest data size per non-final fragment; for MTU 1500 and a 20-byte header it is 1480 bytes.

title: IPv6 address space
description: About 340 undecillion addresses, compared with about 4.3 billion (2^32) for IPv4.

title: IPv6 packet length
description: The fixed base header is always 40 bytes; the payload length field counts extension headers plus upper-layer data.

title: Interface identifier size
description: For the standard /64 LAN prefix the interface identifier is 64 bits, used by SLAAC.

title: Port space
description: Port numbers are 16-bit fields, giving 65,536 ports per transport protocol.

title: Ephemeral range size
description: The IANA dynamic/private range 49152 to 65535 holds 16,384 ports.

title: TCP connection identifier
description: A TCP connection is uniquely identified by this 4-tuple (a pair of sockets).
plainText: (source IP, source port, destination IP, destination port)

title: Handshake acknowledgements
description: Each SYN consumes one sequence number, so it is acknowledged with ISN + 1.
plainText: SYN-ACK ack = x + 1; final ACK ack = y + 1

title: TIME_WAIT timer
description: The active closer waits twice the maximum segment lifetime before the connection is fully closed.

title: First data byte
description: Because the SYN uses the ISN, application data starts numbering at ISN + 1.
plainText: first data byte sequence number = ISN + 1

title: Retransmission timeout
description: Jacobson's formula sets the timeout from the smoothed RTT plus a safety margin of four deviations.

title: Smoothed RTT (EWMA)
description: Each new RTT sample moves the estimate by one-eighth of the difference.

title: Window-limited throughput
description: A TCP sender can deliver at most one window of data per round-trip time.

title: Multiplicative decrease
description: On loss, TCP halves the threshold (and cwnd, or resets cwnd to 1 on timeout).

title: Token bucket burst
description: Maximum time a token bucket of capacity C with token rate p can send at peak rate M.

title: FTP connection count
description: One persistent control connection plus a fresh data connection for each of the n files or listings transferred.

title: File transfer time
description: Approximate time to move a file of F bytes over a path with throughput R bit/s, ignoring setup delays.

title: Base64 encoded size
description: Number of base64 characters produced from n bytes of binary data, ignoring line breaks.

title: Base64 overhead
description: Every 3 bytes become 4 characters, so encoded attachments grow by about one third.

title: Client-server distribution time
description: Minimum time for one server to deliver a file of F bits to N clients; grows linearly with N.

title: P2P distribution time
description: Minimum P2P distribution time, where peer upload capacity sum u_i grows with the number of peers.
plainText: D_p2p >= max(F / u_s, F / d_min, NF / (u_s + sum u_i))

title: Iterative DNS lookup time
description: Time for a lookup with an empty cache when the local server queries each level of the hierarchy in turn.

title: Port number space
description: TCP and UDP port fields are 16 bits wide, giving port numbers 0 to 65535.

title: Connection identifier
description: The five-tuple that uniquely identifies each connection, letting one server port serve many clients.
plainText: (source IP, source port, destination IP, destination port, protocol)

title: Link utilisation from SNMP
description: Percentage utilisation of an interface computed from two readings of its ifInOctets or ifOutOctets counter.
plainText: U = 8 x delta octets / (delta t x ifSpeed) x 100%

title: Samples per day
description: Number of polling samples a monitor collects per day; MRTG's 300 s interval gives 288.

title: Measured throughput
description: Average bit rate from B captured bytes over a capture interval of t seconds, as shown in Wireshark statistics.

title: RSA modulus and totient
description: The public modulus and Euler's totient from which the RSA exponents are derived.

title: RSA key relation
description: The private exponent d is the modular inverse of the public exponent e.

title: RSA encrypt and decrypt
description: Encryption uses the public key (e, n) and decryption uses the private key (d, n).
latex: c = m^{e} \bmod n, \quad m = c^{d} \bmod n
plainText: c = m^e mod n, m = c^d mod n

title: Diffie-Hellman shared key
description: Both parties arrive at g^(ab) mod p without transmitting it.
plainText: K = B^a mod p = A^b mod p

title: Symmetric key count
description: Number of distinct secret keys for every pair of n users to communicate privately.

title: RSA signature generation
description: The message digest is raised to the signer's private exponent.

title: RSA signature verification
description: The verifier uses the signer's public key and compares with a freshly computed hash.

title: Radix-64 expansion
description: Every 3 binary bytes become 4 ASCII characters, about 33% larger.

title: TLS master secret
description: TLS 1.2 derives the session's master secret from the pre-master secret and both hello randoms.

title: HTTPS connection setup time
description: One RTT for the TCP handshake plus k RTTs for TLS (k = 2 for TLS 1.2, 1 for TLS 1.3) before the first request.

title: IPsec tunnel packet size
description: Tunnel mode adds a new IPv4 header and the ESP header, trailer and integrity check value to the original packet.
latex: L_{tunnel} = L_{orig} + 20 + L_{ESP\ hdr} + L_{trailer} + L_{ICV}

title: WEP encryption
description: WEP XORs the message and its CRC-32 ICV with an RC4 keystream seeded by the IV and shared key.

title: WEP IV space
description: The small 24-bit IV space makes IV and keystream reuse inevitable on a busy network.

title: Birthday bound for IV collision
description: With random IVs a repeat is more likely than not after only about 4800 frames.

title: Shannon and Nyquist capacity
description: B bandwidth in Hz, S/N as a power ratio (not dB), L signal levels.
plainText: C = B log₂(1 + S/N);  noiseless C = 2B log₂L

title: Subnetting
description: h host bits, s borrowed bits; two addresses are the network and broadcast addresses.

title: Stop-and-wait efficiency
description: Fraction of time the link carries new data when one frame is outstanding.

title: Hamming check bits
description: m data bits need the smallest r satisfying the inequality for single-error correction.

title: RSA
description: p, q primes; (e, n) is the public key and (d, n) the private key.
latex: n = pq,\ \varphi = (p-1)(q-1),\ ed \equiv 1 \pmod{\varphi},\ c = m^e \bmod n
plainText: n = pq; φ = (p−1)(q−1); ed ≡ 1 mod φ; c = m^e mod n

title: Full mesh links
description: Number of dedicated duplex links needed to connect n devices in a fully connected mesh.

title: Mesh ports per device
description: Each device in a full mesh needs one I/O port for every other device.

title: Star links
description: A star topology of n devices needs one link from each device to the central hub or switch.

title: Hamming redundant bits
description: Smallest r satisfying this gives the number of parity bits needed to correct a single-bit error in m data bits.

title: Minimum distance rules
description: Relates the minimum Hamming distance of a code to how many errors it can detect or correct.
plainText: detect s: d_min >= s + 1; correct t: d_min >= 2t + 1

title: CRC codeword
description: The transmitted CRC codeword is exactly divisible by the degree-r generator G(x).
plainText: T(x) = x^r D(x) + (x^r D(x) mod G(x))

title: Usable hosts per subnet
description: h is the number of host bits; the all-zeros network address and all-ones broadcast address are excluded.

title: Number of subnets
description: s is the number of bits borrowed from the host part; /26 from a /24 borrows 2 bits and gives 4 subnets.

title: Addresses in a CIDR block
description: Total addresses covered by prefix length n, including network and broadcast addresses.
plainText: N = 2^(32 − n) addresses in a /n block

title: Subnet block size
description: m is the value of the last non-255 mask octet; subnets start at multiples of B, e.g. mask .192 gives a block size of 64.

title: TCP header length
description: The 4-bit HLEN field counts 32-bit words, so values 5 to 15 give a header of 20 to 60 bytes.

title: UDP length
description: The UDP length field covers the fixed 8-byte header plus the payload.

title: Acknowledgement number
description: TCP acknowledges cumulatively by naming the next byte it expects to receive.
plainText: ACK = sequence number + number of data bytes received

title: Non-persistent HTTP time
description: Total time to fetch a base file and N referenced objects when each object uses a new TCP connection serially.

title: Persistent HTTP time
description: With a persistent connection and no pipelining, only the first object pays the TCP handshake RTT.

title: Pipelined HTTP time
description: With persistence and pipelining, all referenced objects are requested together and arrive in roughly one extra RTT.

title: Availability
description: Fraction of time a system is operational, from mean time between failures and mean time to repair.

title: Annual loss expectancy
description: Expected yearly loss from a threat, used to justify the cost of a security control.

title: Qualitative risk
description: Risk is zero if any factor is absent, e.g. a threat with no vulnerability to exploit.
plainText: Risk = Threat x Vulnerability x Impact

title: Initial partition
description: The partition method begins by separating accepting states from non-accepting states.

title: State equivalence
description: Two states are equivalent when no input string leads one to acceptance and the other to rejection.
plainText: p ≡ q iff for all w, δ̂(p, w) ∈ F ⇔ δ̂(q, w) ∈ F

title: Table-filling pairs
description: Number of unordered state pairs the table-filling method must examine for an n-state DFA.

title: Hopcroft complexity
description: Hopcroft's partition-refinement algorithm is the fastest standard DFA minimization method.
plainText: Hopcroft's algorithm: O(k · n log n) for n states, k symbols

title: Arden's theorem
description: Solves the state equations of a finite automaton to obtain an equivalent regular expression.
latex: R = Q + RP \ \Rightarrow\ R = QP^{*}\quad (\varepsilon \notin L(P))
plainText: If R = Q + RP and ε ∉ P, then R = QP*

title: Positive closure
description: Relates one-or-more repetition to the Kleene star.
plainText: r+ = r r*; r* = ε + r+

title: State elimination rule
description: Removing state k replaces every path p → k → q with a single RE-labelled edge.

title: Star identities
description: Common identities used to simplify regular expressions.

title: Pumping lemma conditions
description: Every string of length at least p in a regular language can be split and pumped this way.
plainText: |xy| ≤ p, |y| ≥ 1, xy^i z ∈ L for all i ≥ 0

title: Pigeonhole bound
description: Explains why the pumping length p can be taken as the number of DFA states.
plainText: |s| ≥ p ⇒ p + 1 states visited in a p-state DFA ⇒ some state repeats

title: Complement closure
description: Obtained from a complete DFA by swapping final and non-final states, so regular languages are closed under complement.

title: Chomsky Normal Form
description: Every production has either exactly two variables or a single terminal on the right, giving binary parse trees.

title: CNF derivation length
description: A string of length n needs n − 1 applications of A → BC and n applications of A → a in a CNF grammar.

title: Greibach Normal Form
description: Every body starts with one terminal followed only by variables, so each derivation step emits exactly one terminal.

title: PDA 7-tuple
description: A PDA has states, input and stack alphabets, a transition function, a start state, an initial stack symbol and final states.
plainText: M = (Q, Σ, Γ, δ, q0, Z0, F)

title: PDA transition function
description: Each move depends on state, an input symbol or ε, and the stack top, and may lead to several (state, stack string) choices.
plainText: δ: Q × (Σ ∪ {ε}) × Γ → finite subsets of Q × Γ*

title: Acceptance by empty stack
description: A string is accepted by empty stack when all input is consumed and the stack is empty, in any state.

title: CFL pumping lemma
description: Every long enough string in a CFL has two nearby pieces v and x that can be pumped together while staying in the language.
latex: s = uvwxy,\ |vwx| \le p,\ |vx| \ge 1,\ uv^i w x^i y \in L
plainText: s = uvwxy, |vwx| ≤ p, |vx| ≥ 1, uvⁱwxⁱy ∈ L for all i ≥ 0

title: Intersection counterexample
description: Two context-free languages whose intersection is not context-free, showing CFLs are not closed under intersection.
latex: \{a^n b^n c^m\} \cap \{a^m b^n c^n\} = \{a^n b^n c^n\}

title: CYK table and time
description: The CYK membership test fills one cell per substring of the input and runs in cubic time for a fixed CNF grammar.

title: Recursive = RE ∩ co-RE
description: A language is decidable exactly when both it and its complement are Turing-recognisable.
plainText: L recursive ⟺ L and complement(L) both RE

title: Unary addition TM
description: Replacing the separator 0 by 1 and erasing the last 1 turns 1ᵐ01ⁿ into 1^(m+n).

title: Proper subtraction
description: Monus, a total function on natural numbers that a TM computes by cancelling 1s pairwise.

title: Multi-tape transition
description: A k-tape TM reads all k heads, then writes and moves each head independently.
plainText: δ: Q × Γ^k → Q × Γ^k × {L, R, S}^k

title: Multi-track alphabet size
description: A k-track tape is an ordinary tape whose symbols are k-tuples, one component per track.

title: Simulation slowdowns
description: Cost of simulating each variant on a single-tape deterministic TM running t(n) steps.

title: Transition encoding
description: Binary code of δ(qi, Xj) = (qk, Xl, Dm); transitions are separated by 11.

title: Mapping reduction
description: A computable map sends yes-instances of A to yes-instances of B and no-instances to no-instances.
plainText: A ≤m B ⟺ (w ∈ A ⟺ f(w) ∈ B) for a computable f

title: Class P
description: Languages decided by a deterministic TM in time bounded by some polynomial of the input length.
plainText: P = union over k ≥ 1 of TIME(n^k)

title: Complexity class inclusions
description: Known inclusions; P ≠ EXPTIME is proved, but whether P = NP is open.

title: Proving NP-completeness
description: Show membership in NP and a polynomial-time reduction from a known NP-complete problem.
latex: B \in \mathrm{NP},\; A \text{ NPC},\; A \le_p B \Rightarrow B \text{ NPC}
plainText: B ∈ NP, A NP-complete, A ≤p B ⇒ B NP-complete

title: Frame-buffer size
description: Memory needed to store one full screen of H by V pixels at n bits per pixel.
plainText: Size (bytes) = H x V x n / 8

title: Colours from bit depth
description: Number of distinct values a pixel can hold with n bits per pixel.

title: Horizontal scan rate
description: Scan lines drawn per second, ignoring retrace time, e.g. 768 x 60 = 46,080 lines/s.

title: Aspect ratio
description: Ratio of horizontal to vertical size of the display, e.g. 1920 / 1080 = 16:9.

title: Pixel rate
description: Number of pixels the video controller must read out per second, ignoring retrace.
plainText: Pixel rate = H x V x refresh rate

title: Time per pixel
description: Upper bound on the time available to fetch and display each pixel.
plainText: t_pixel = 1 / (H x V x refresh rate)

title: Video memory bandwidth
description: Bytes per second the frame buffer must supply to refresh the screen at n bits per pixel.
plainText: B = H x V x refresh rate x n/8 bytes per second

title: Reflection about y = x
description: Swaps coordinates so that (x, y) becomes (y, x).

title: x-direction shear
description: Shifts each point horizontally by an amount proportional to its y coordinate.

title: Rotation about a pivot
description: Composite matrix that rotates by θ about the pivot point (xr, yr).

title: Scaling about a fixed point
description: Composite matrix that scales an object while keeping (xf, yf) stationary.

title: Viewport x coordinate
description: Maps a world x coordinate in the window to the corresponding viewport x coordinate.

title: Viewport y coordinate
description: Maps a world y coordinate in the window to the corresponding viewport y coordinate.

title: Scale factor
description: Ratio of viewport width to window width; sy is the ratio of heights.

title: Window-to-viewport matrix
description: Composite form of the viewing transformation: shift, scale, shift.

title: Boundary intersection
description: Intersection of a line with a vertical edge x = xb or a horizontal edge y = yb in Cohen–Sutherland.
plainText: y = y1 + m(xb − x1); x = x1 + (yb − y1)/m

title: Parametric line
description: Liang–Barsky representation of the segment for 0 ≤ t ≤ 1.
plainText: x = x1 + t·Δx, y = y1 + t·Δy

title: Liang–Barsky parameters
description: Left and right edge terms; bottom and top use −Δy, y1 − ywmin and Δy, ywmax − y1.
latex: p_1=-\Delta x,\ q_1=x_1-xw_{min};\ p_2=\Delta x,\ q_2=xw_{max}-x_1
plainText: p1 = −Δx, q1 = x1 − xwmin; p2 = Δx, q2 = xwmax − x1 (y edges analogous)

title: Entry and exit parameters
description: The visible segment runs from t_entry to t_exit; if t_entry > t_exit the line is rejected.
plainText: t_entry = max(0, qk/pk for pk < 0), t_exit = min(1, qk/pk for pk > 0)

title: Reflection about xy-plane
description: Negates the coordinate perpendicular to the mirror plane; the other planes work the same way.

title: Shear relative to z-axis
description: Slides x and y in proportion to z while z is unchanged.
plainText: x' = x + a·z, y' = y + b·z, z' = z

title: Rotation about arbitrary axis
description: Align the axis with z, rotate by θ, then undo the alignment in reverse order.

title: Inverse of a composite
description: Invert each factor and reverse their order.

title: Viewing-frame axes
description: Builds the orthonormal camera frame from the view-plane normal and the view-up vector.
latex: n=\frac{N}{|N|},\quad u=\frac{V\times n}{|V\times n|},\quad v=n\times u
plainText: n = N/|N|, u = (V × n)/|V × n|, v = n × u

title: World-to-viewing matrix
description: Translates the view reference point to the origin, then rotates u, v, n onto x, y, z.

title: Pipeline order
description: Modelling, world, viewing, projection, normalised and device coordinates in sequence.
latex: MC\to WC\to VC\to PC\to NC\to DC
plainText: MC → WC → VC → projection → NC → DC

title: Perspective projection
description: COP at the origin and view plane at z = d; division by z produces foreshortening.

title: Oblique projection
description: Depth is drawn at angle φ scaled by L = 1/tan α (L = 1 cavalier, 1/2 cabinet).
plainText: x_p = x + L·z·cos φ, y_p = y + L·z·sin φ

title: Orthographic projection
description: Projectors perpendicular to the xy view plane, so the z-coordinate is simply discarded.
plainText: x_p = x, y_p = y, z dropped

title: General perspective (Hearn & Baker)
description: Projection reference point at z_prp on the z-axis and view plane at z_vp; y_p is analogous.

title: Subset-construction bound
description: Each DFA state is a subset of NFA states; usually far fewer are reachable.

title: Regular pumping lemma
description: Used to prove a language is NOT regular by showing some pumped string leaves L.
plainText: w = xyz, |xy| ≤ p, |y| ≥ 1, xy^i z ∈ L for all i ≥ 0

title: 2D rotation
description: Anticlockwise rotation about the origin by θ.
latex: x' = x\cos\theta - y\sin\theta,\qquad y' = x\sin\theta + y\cos\theta
plainText: x' = x cos θ − y sin θ;  y' = x sin θ + y cos θ

title: Window-to-viewport
description: The same form maps y; unequal s_x and s_y distort the aspect ratio.
latex: x_v = xv_{min} + (x_w - xw_{min})\,s_x,\quad s_x = \frac{xv_{max} - xv_{min}}{xw_{max} - xw_{min}}

title: Perspective projection
description: Centre of projection at the origin, view plane at z = d; farther points shrink.

title: DFA 5-tuple
description: A DFA has exactly one next state for every state and input symbol.
plainText: M = (Q, Σ, δ, q0, F), δ: Q × Σ → Q

title: Extended transition function
description: Extends δ from single symbols to whole strings and defines the accepted language.

title: NFA transition function
description: An NFA (with optional ε-moves) maps each state and symbol to a set of possible next states.

title: Subset construction bound
description: Each DFA state is a subset of the n NFA states, so at most 2^n DFA states are possible.
plainText: DFA states ≤ 2^n for an n-state NFA

title: CFG 4-tuple
description: A context-free grammar consists of variables, terminals, productions with a single variable on the left, and a start symbol.

title: Derivation step
description: One derivation step replaces a single variable by the body of one of its productions, independent of its context.
plainText: αAβ ⇒ αγβ if A → γ ∈ P

title: Language of a grammar
description: The language of a grammar is every terminal string derivable from the start symbol in zero or more steps.

title: TM 7-tuple
description: States, input alphabet, tape alphabet, transition function, start state, blank symbol and final states.
plainText: M = (Q, Σ, Γ, δ, q0, B, F)

title: TM transition function
description: From a state and scanned symbol, the TM picks a next state, a symbol to write and a head direction.
plainText: δ: Q × Γ → Q × Γ × {L, R}

title: Language accepted by a TM
description: A string is accepted when some sequence of moves from the start ID reaches a final state.
latex: L(M) = \{ w : q_0 w \vdash^* \alpha\, p\, \beta,\; p \in F \}
plainText: L(M) = { w : q0 w ⊢* α p β, p ∈ F }

title: World to NDC normalization
description: Maps a world x coordinate inside the window to the 0 to 1 normalized range.

title: NDC to device coordinates
description: Converts normalized coordinates into integer pixel positions on a W by H device.

title: Viewing pipeline composition
description: A point passes through modelling, viewing, projection and viewport transforms, applied right to left.
latex: P_{device} = M_{viewport} \cdot M_{proj} \cdot M_{view} \cdot M_{model} \cdot P
plainText: P_device = M_viewport * M_proj * M_view * M_model * P

title: Translation matrix
description: Homogeneous 3 × 3 matrix that shifts a point by (tx, ty).

title: Rotation about origin
description: Counter-clockwise rotation of a point by angle θ about the origin.
plainText: x' = x cos θ − y sin θ, y' = x sin θ + y cos θ

title: Scaling matrix
description: Scales x by sx and y by sy about the origin; uniform when sx = sy.

title: Fixed-point scaling
description: Scaling that keeps the point (xf, yf) stationary; the y equation is analogous.

title: 3D translation matrix
description: Shifts every point by (t_x, t_y, t_z); the offsets occupy the fourth column.
plainText: x' = x + tx, y' = y + ty, z' = z + tz

title: Rotation about z-axis
description: The 2D rotation extended to 3D with z unchanged; cycle x→y→z→x for the other axes.
plainText: x' = x cos θ − y sin θ, y' = x sin θ + y cos θ, z' = z

title: Rotation about y-axis
description: Note the apparently swapped sine signs, which come from the cyclic permutation.
plainText: x' = x cos θ + z sin θ, z' = −x sin θ + z cos θ, y' = y

title: Fixed-point scaling
description: Scales an object in place about (x_f, y_f, z_f) without moving that point.
plainText: Sf = T(xf, yf, zf) · S(sx, sy, sz) · T(−xf, −yf, −zf)

title: Array stack conditions
description: Tests used before pop (underflow) and push (overflow) in an array stack.
plainText: top = -1 means empty; top = MAX - 1 means full

title: Postfix operator step
description: The first value popped is the right operand, the second is the left operand.
plainText: b = pop(), a = pop(), push(a op b)

title: Stack operation cost
description: All stack operations touch only the top, so they run in constant time.

title: Circular increment
description: Advances an index around the ring so freed slots at the start are reused.

title: Circular queue full
description: The next slot after rear is the front, so no more elements can be inserted.

title: Array list shift cost
description: Why insertion and deletion in an array list are O(n) in the worst case.
plainText: Inserting at index k in an n-element array list shifts n - k elements

title: Node size
description: k = 1 for a singly linked node and k = 2 for a doubly linked node.
plainText: Node size = data + k × pointer size

title: Head vs tail insertion
description: Tail insertion must walk the whole list unless a tail pointer is maintained.
plainText: Head insertion O(1); tail insertion O(n) without a tail pointer

title: Reversal cost
description: Each node's link is reversed once using the three pointers prev, curr and next.
plainText: In-place reversal: O(n) time, O(1) extra space

title: Maximum nodes
description: Reached by a perfect binary tree with the root at level 0.

title: Minimum height
description: The shortest possible binary tree holding n nodes.

title: Leaves in a full tree
description: Holds for full (strictly) binary trees where every node has 0 or 2 children.

title: Array indices
description: Index relations for a binary tree stored in a 0-based array.

title: Balance factor
description: An AVL node is balanced when its subtree heights differ by at most one.

title: Minimum nodes of height h
description: Fewest nodes an AVL tree of height h can have: 1, 2, 4, 7, 12, 20, ...

title: AVL height bound
description: Guarantees O(log n) worst-case search, insertion and deletion.

title: Merge sort recurrence
description: Two half-size subproblems plus a linear merge give n log n time in every case.

title: Heap index formulas (0-based)
description: Lets a complete binary tree be stored in an array with no pointers.

title: Radix sort time
description: d stable bucket passes over n keys with k possible digit values.

title: Shell sort with Knuth gaps
description: Knuth's gap sequence gives roughly n to the power 1.5 behaviour.

title: Binary search comparisons
description: Worst-case number of comparisons for binary search over n sorted elements.

title: Division hash and load factor
description: The division method maps a key to a slot; the load factor measures how full the table is.
plainText: h(k) = k mod m, α = n/m

title: Open-addressing probe sequences
description: Linear, quadratic and double hashing probe sequences for i = 0, 1, 2, ...

title: Sequential search average
description: Average comparisons for a successful linear search when each key is equally likely.

title: Maximum edges
description: Upper bound on edges in a simple graph with n vertices.

title: Handshaking lemma
description: Every undirected edge adds one to the degree of each of its two endpoints.

title: Warshall recurrence
description: Path i to j exists through vertices 1..k if it existed before or goes i to k to j; O(V³) overall.

title: Edge relaxation
description: The update used by Dijkstra and Bellman-Ford whenever a shorter path to v through u is found.

title: MST edge count
description: Any spanning tree of a connected graph with V vertices has exactly V - 1 edges.

title: MST algorithm times
description: Prim with a binary heap and Kruskal dominated by sorting the edges.
latex: T_{Prim} = O(E \log V),\; T_{Kruskal} = O(E \log E)
plainText: Prim O(E log V), Kruskal O(E log E)

title: Dijkstra time
description: Each vertex is extracted once and each edge relaxed once.
plainText: O((V + E) log V) with a heap, O(V²) with an array

title: Attribute closure
description: The closure of X is every attribute that X determines under the given dependencies.
plainText: X+ = set of attributes A such that F implies X -> A

title: Superkey test
description: Compute X+ and compare it with the full attribute set to test whether X is a superkey.
latex: X \text{ is a superkey of } R \iff X^{+} = R
plainText: X is a superkey iff X+ contains all attributes of R

title: Superkey count (one key)
description: With n attributes and one single-attribute candidate key, every superset of that key is a superkey.

title: Lossless-join test
description: A binary decomposition is lossless when the shared attributes are a superkey of at least one part.
latex: R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_1 \ \text{ or } \ R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_2
plainText: (R1 intersect R2) -> R1 or (R1 intersect R2) -> R2

title: 3NF condition
description: 3NF allows a non-superkey determinant only when the dependent attribute belongs to some candidate key.
latex: \forall X \to A:\ X \text{ superkey or } A \text{ prime}
plainText: For every nontrivial X -> A, X is a superkey or A is prime

title: BCNF condition
description: BCNF requires every determinant of a nontrivial dependency to be a superkey.
plainText: Every nontrivial X -> Y has X+ = R

title: Cartesian product size
description: A cross join pairs every row of R with every row of S.

title: Full outer join size
description: A full outer join returns the inner-join rows plus every unmatched row of each table padded with NULLs.
plainText: Full outer rows = inner rows + unmatched R + unmatched S

title: Left outer join bound
description: Every row of the left table appears at least once in a left outer join.
plainText: Left outer join rows >= rows of R

title: Query cost
description: Query cost counts block transfers and disk seeks weighted by their times.
plainText: Cost = b x tT + S x tS

title: Nested-loop join
description: In the worst case the inner relation is scanned once for every tuple of the outer relation.
plainText: n_r x b_s + b_r block transfers

title: Block nested-loop join
description: The inner relation is scanned once per block of the outer relation instead of once per tuple.
plainText: b_r x b_s + b_r block transfers

title: Hash join
description: Both relations are read and written once when partitioning and read again when probing.
plainText: Hash join about 3(b_r + b_s) block transfers

title: Wait-die rule
description: Non-preemptive: an older requester waits, a younger requester is rolled back and restarted with its original timestamp.
latex: \text{Wait-die: } TS(T_i) < TS(T_j) \Rightarrow T_i \text{ waits, else } T_i \text{ dies}
plainText: Wait-die: if TS(Ti) < TS(Tj) then Ti waits, else Ti is rolled back

title: Wound-wait rule
description: Preemptive: an older requester forces the younger lock holder to roll back, a younger requester waits.
latex: \text{Wound-wait: } TS(T_i) < TS(T_j) \Rightarrow T_j \text{ rolled back, else } T_i \text{ waits}
plainText: Wound-wait: if TS(Ti) < TS(Tj) then Tj is rolled back, else Ti waits

title: Deadlock detection
description: With single-instance locks, a cycle in the wait-for graph is both necessary and sufficient for deadlock.
plainText: Deadlock iff the wait-for graph has a cycle

title: Redo rule
description: A committed transaction's updates are reapplied using the new values so that its effects are durable.
plainText: Redo Ti if the log contains both <Ti start> and <Ti commit>

title: Undo rule
description: An incomplete transaction is rolled back by restoring old values, scanning the log backward.
latex: \text{undo}(T_i) \text{ if } \langle T_i\ \text{start}\rangle \text{ in log but no commit or abort}
plainText: Undo Ti if the log has <Ti start> but no <Ti commit> or <Ti abort>

title: Checkpoint scan range
description: Checkpoints bound recovery work, since earlier committed transactions are already on disk.
latex: \text{Scan range} = \text{log records from last checkpoint (and its list } L\text{) to end}
plainText: Recovery scans from the last checkpoint (and its active list L) to the end of the log

title: Turnaround time
description: Total time a process spends in the system from arrival to completion.

title: Waiting time
description: Time a process spends in the ready queue, excluding its own execution.

title: Response time
description: Delay until a process first gets the CPU; the key metric for interactive systems.

title: Processes after n forks
description: Each unconditional fork doubles the number of running processes.

title: Semaphore final value
description: Net effect of a sequence of wait and signal operations on a counting semaphore.
plainText: S_final = S0 - P count + V count

title: Blocked processes
description: In the blocking implementation a negative value counts the processes queued on the semaphore.

title: Banker's need matrix
description: Remaining resources each process may still request before finishing.

title: Safety-check step
description: A process whose need fits in Work can finish and release everything it holds.
plainText: If Need_i <= Work then Work += Allocation_i

title: Deadlock-free resource count
description: Minimum units of a single resource type that make deadlock impossible for n processes each needing up to k units.

title: Effective access time
description: Average memory access time under demand paging with page-fault rate p.

title: EAT with TLB
description: A TLB miss costs one extra memory access to read the page-table entry.

title: Page-table size
description: Number of pages (virtual space over page size) times the bytes per page-table entry.

title: Proportional allocation
description: Each process gets frames in proportion to its size out of m available frames.

title: Pointers per index block
description: Number of block addresses that fit in one indirect (index) block.

title: Inode maximum file size
description: Sum of blocks reachable through direct, single, double and triple indirect pointers, times block size.
plainText: Max = (direct + P + P² + P³) × block size

title: Blocks for a file
description: Number of data blocks a file occupies; the unused tail of the last block is internal fragmentation.

title: Disk access time
description: Total time to service one disk request.

title: Average rotational latency
description: On average the desired sector is half a revolution away.

title: CHS to logical block
description: Maps cylinder, head and 1-based sector to a logical block number.

title: Bit-vector size
description: One bit is needed for every block on the disk.

title: Permission digit
description: Each octal digit of a UNIX mode is the sum of read (4), write (2) and execute (1) bits for one class.

title: umask default
description: New files start from 666 and directories from 777, with the umask bits removed (022 gives 644 and 755).

title: Big-O definition
description: f = O(g) when some constant multiple of g bounds f from some point on.
plainText: f(n) ≤ c·g(n) for all n ≥ n₀

title: Binary-tree node bound
description: h is the height with a single root at height 0.

title: Waiting and turnaround
description: Average these over all processes to compare scheduling algorithms.
latex: TAT = C - A,\qquad WT = TAT - BT
plainText: TAT = completion − arrival;  WT = TAT − burst

title: Effective access time
description: p page-fault rate, t_m memory access time, t_f page-fault service time.

title: Disk access time
description: rps is revolutions per second; average rotational latency is half a revolution.
plainText: t = seek + half a rotation + bytes/transfer rate

title: Big-O definition
description: Upper bound: beyond some n0, f never exceeds a constant multiple of g.
plainText: f(n) = O(g(n)) if f(n) <= c·g(n) for all n >= n0

title: Big-Theta definition
description: Tight bound: f is sandwiched between two constant multiples of g.
plainText: c1·g(n) <= f(n) <= c2·g(n) for n >= n0

title: Growth-rate order
description: Standard ordering of common complexity classes from slowest to fastest growing.
plainText: 1 < log n < n < n log n < n² < 2ⁿ < n!

title: Master theorem form
description: d < log_b a gives Θ(n^log_b a), d = log_b a gives Θ(n^d log n), d > log_b a gives Θ(n^d).
plainText: T(n) = aT(n/b) + Θ(n^d); compare d with log_b a

title: Triangular loop count
description: Iterations of a nested loop whose inner bound is the outer index; O(n²).

title: Comparisons of simple sorts
description: Selection sort always makes this many comparisons; insertion and bubble sort make it in the worst case.

title: Insertion sort best case
description: On already sorted input insertion sort (and bubble sort with a flag) needs only n - 1 comparisons.

title: Quick sort recurrences
description: Balanced partitions give O(n log n) while always-extreme pivots give O(n²).
latex: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n \Rightarrow O(n\log n);\; T(n) = T(n-1) + n \Rightarrow O(n^2)
plainText: Balanced: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n -> O(n log n); unbalanced: T(n) = T(n-1) + n -> O(n²)

title: Weak entity key
description: A weak entity is identified by its owner's primary key combined with its own discriminator.
plainText: PK of weak entity = PK of owner + partial key

title: M:N relationship key
description: An M:N relationship maps to its own table keyed by the primary keys of both participating entity sets.
plainText: Key of an M:N relationship table = union of both entity keys

title: Serial schedules
description: Each ordering of the n transactions, run one after another, is a distinct serial schedule.
plainText: Number of serial schedules of n transactions = n!

title: Total possible schedules
description: Counts all interleavings that keep each transaction's own operations in order; e.g. two transactions of 2 operations each give 4!/(2!2!) = 6.

title: Conflict serializability test
description: Add an edge Ti -> Tj for every conflicting pair where Ti acts first; any cycle means the schedule is not conflict serializable.
plainText: Conflict serializable iff precedence graph has no cycle

title: Multiprogramming CPU utilisation
description: Probability that at least one of n independent processes (each I/O-bound a fraction p of the time) is ready to use the CPU.

title: Time-sharing worst-case wait
description: With n ready users and quantum q, a user waits at most (n - 1) quanta before getting the CPU again.

title: Relocation and limit
description: Dynamic relocation adds the base register to each valid logical address and traps if the limit is exceeded.
plainText: PA = relocation + LA, if 0 ≤ LA < limit

title: Paging address split
description: The page number indexes the page table and the offset is copied unchanged into the physical address.
latex: p = \lfloor LA / S \rfloor,\; d = LA \bmod S
plainText: p = floor(LA / S), d = LA mod S

title: Physical address from frame
description: Once the page table gives frame f, the physical address is the frame base plus the offset.

title: Bits in page number
description: With a 2^m-byte logical space and 2^n-byte pages, the page number uses m − n bits and the offset n bits.

title: Team communication paths
description: Number of pairwise communication channels in a team of n people, the basis of Brooks' law.

title: Sprints to finish a backlog
description: Estimated number of sprints to complete the remaining backlog at the team's measured velocity.

title: Risk exposure (spiral model)
description: Probability of a risk occurring times the loss if it occurs, used to rank risks in each spiral loop.

title: Development productivity
description: Thousand lines of code delivered per person-month, used to compare work with and without tools.

title: Productivity gain from CASE
description: Percentage improvement in productivity after introducing CASE support.

title: Return on tool investment
description: Net benefit of a CASE tool relative to its purchase, training and support cost.

title: Allowed downtime from availability
description: Converts an availability requirement into the maximum permitted downtime per year.

title: Throughput requirement
description: Measurable form of a speed requirement, stating how many transactions must be processed per unit time.

title: Probability of failure on demand
description: Reliability metric for systems used on demand, such as a protection system.

title: Requirement specificity
description: Fraction of requirements that all reviewers interpreted identically; closer to 1 means less ambiguity.

title: Functional completeness
description: Unique function requirements divided by the number of inputs times states specified.

title: Requirements volatility
description: Percentage of requirements added, deleted or modified over a period, a measure of requirements stability.

title: Traceability coverage
description: Percentage of requirements linked in the RTM to design, code and test cases.

title: Interfaces: point-to-point vs repository
description: Shows why a shared repository reduces the number of data interfaces among n subsystems.
plainText: Point-to-point interfaces = n(n-1)/2; via repository = n

title: Pipeline latency
description: Time for one item to pass through a sequential pipe-and-filter chain of k filters.

title: Pipeline throughput
description: In a concurrent pipeline the slowest filter is the bottleneck that limits items processed per unit time.

title: Series availability of tiers
description: A request that must pass through every tier succeeds only if all tiers are up, so availabilities multiply.
plainText: A = A1 x A2 x ... x Ak

title: Availability of replicated servers
description: With m independent replicas the service fails only if all replicas fail at once.

title: Amdahl's law
description: Maximum speedup on N processors when only fraction p of the work can run in parallel.

title: P2P vs client-server links
description: Number of connections needed when n nodes are fully interconnected versus all connected to one server.
plainText: P2P links = n(n-1)/2; client-server links = n

title: Rate-monotonic utilisation bound
description: Periodic tasks with compute time Ci and period Ti are guaranteed schedulable by rate-monotonic priority if U is within this bound (0.780 for 3 tasks).

title: EDF utilisation bound
description: Earliest-deadline-first scheduling meets all deadlines of independent periodic tasks whenever total utilisation does not exceed 100%.

title: Reuse level
description: Fraction of a system delivered by reused components, a basic CBSE productivity indicator.
plainText: Reuse level = reused size / total size x 100%

title: Sequential composition reliability
description: When every composed component must work for the result to be correct, reliabilities multiply.
plainText: R = R1 x R2 x ... x Rk

title: Cyclomatic complexity
description: Gives the number of linearly independent paths and the maximum number of basis-path tests.
plainText: V(G) = E - N + 2P = predicate nodes + 1 = regions

title: Statement coverage
description: The weakest white-box coverage measure, reported by tools such as JaCoCo or gcov.
plainText: Statement coverage = statements executed / total statements x 100%

title: BVA test count
description: Number of boundary value test cases needed for n independent input variables.
plainText: Standard BVA = 4n + 1, robustness = 6n + 1, worst case = 5^n tests for n variables

title: Defect density
description: Normalises defect counts by size so that modules and releases can be compared.

title: Defect removal efficiency
description: Fraction of all defects removed before delivery; the ideal value is 1.

title: Basic COCOMO effort
description: Organic 2.4/1.05, semi-detached 3.0/1.12, embedded 3.6/1.20.

title: Basic COCOMO duration
description: The exponent d is 0.38 organic, 0.35 semi-detached and 0.32 embedded.

title: Average staffing
description: Gives the average number of full-time people over the project schedule.

title: Function points
description: Adjusts unadjusted function points by 14 general system characteristics rated 0 to 5.
plainText: FP = UFP x (0.65 + 0.01 x sum Fi)

title: Communication paths
description: Explains Brooks' law: coordination overhead grows quadratically with team size.

title: Availability
description: Probability that the software is operational when it is needed.

title: Mean time between failures
description: Average time from one failure to the next, including the repair time.

title: Halstead length and volume
description: Size measures from total operators N1, total operands N2 and vocabulary n = n1 + n2.
latex: N = N_1 + N_2,\quad V = N \log_2 n
plainText: N = N1 + N2, V = N log2 n

title: Defects per million opportunities
description: Six Sigma quality corresponds to 3.4 DPMO.

title: Card and Glass system complexity
description: Architectural design metric combining structural (fan-out) and data (I/O variables) complexity.
plainText: S(i) = fout^2, D(i) = v(i) / (fout + 1), C(i) = S(i) + D(i)

title: Semantic versioning
description: Incrementing a field resets all fields to its right to zero.

title: Change failure rate
description: Release-management metric showing how often a deployed change causes a production failure.
plainText: Change failure rate = failed changes / total changes deployed x 100%

title: Delta storage
description: Delta-based version control keeps one full version plus the differences needed to rebuild the others.
plainText: Stored size = size of latest version + sum of reverse deltas

title: Use case points
description: Karner's size estimate: unadjusted use case and actor weights scaled by technical and environmental factors.
plainText: UCP = (UUCW + UAW) x TCF x ECF

title: Unadjusted use case weight
description: Use cases are weighted by transaction count: up to 3 simple, 4 to 7 average, more than 7 complex.
plainText: UUCW = 5 x simple + 10 x average + 15 x complex use cases

title: Technical complexity factor
description: Adjusts size for 13 weighted technical factors such as distribution, performance and reusability.

title: Environmental complexity factor
description: Adjusts size for 8 team and environment factors; a more experienced team gives a smaller ECF.

title: UML 2.5 diagram count
description: UML 2.5 defines seven structural and seven behavioural diagram types, four of the behavioural ones being interaction diagrams.

title: Parts of a conceptual class
description: A conceptual class has a name or image, a definition, and the set of real instances it applies to.

title: Possible binary associations
description: The number of distinct class pairs that could be linked among n conceptual classes, which is why only need-to-know associations are drawn.

title: Link bounds from multiplicity
description: With N source objects and multiplicity lower..upper on the far end, the total links lie between N times each bound.
latex: L_{min} = N \times lower,\quad L_{max} = N \times upper
plainText: L_min = N x lower, L_max = N x upper

title: Many-to-many link limit
description: A * to * association between classes A and B can have at most one link per pair of instances.

title: Postcondition categories
description: Every contract postcondition falls into one of these three categories of domain-object state change.
plainText: Postconditions = instance creation/deletion + attribute modification + associations formed/broken

title: Message nesting depth
description: In Dewey-decimal numbering each extra dot means the message was sent while handling the message numbered by the prefix.
latex: \text{Nesting depth} = \text{number of dots in the sequence number} + 1
plainText: Nesting depth of message = number of dots in its sequence number + 1 (1.2.3 is depth 3)

title: Call plus reply arrows
description: A synchronous call is drawn with a filled arrowhead and, when the return is shown explicitly, a dashed reply arrow back to the caller.
latex: \text{Messages for a synchronous call shown with reply} = 2
plainText: A synchronous call drawn with its reply uses 2 arrows: the call and the dashed return

title: Maximum object links
description: The upper bound on distinct links if every pair of n participating objects needed visibility of each other, which good design avoids.
plainText: Maximum links among n objects in a communication diagram = n(n - 1) / 2

title: GoF pattern count
description: The Gang of Four catalogue of 23 patterns split by purpose into three categories.

title: GRASP pattern count
description: Larman's nine principles for assigning responsibilities to classes while drawing interaction diagrams.
plainText: GRASP = 9 patterns: Expert, Creator, Controller, Low Coupling, High Cohesion, Polymorphism, Pure Fabrication, Indirection, Protected Variations

title: Coupling pairs bound
description: Low Coupling aims to keep actual dependencies far below this maximum number of class pairs.
plainText: Possible coupling pairs among n classes <= n(n - 1) / 2

title: Weighted methods per class
description: A Chidamber-Kemerer metric computed from a design class diagram; a high WMC suggests a class with too many responsibilities.
plainText: Weighted methods per class WMC = sum of complexities c_i of its n methods (c_i = 1 gives the method count)

title: Many-to-many link bound
description: Each object of A can be linked to every object of B at most once, giving at most m times n links.
latex: \text{Links in a 1..* to 1..* association} \le m \times n
plainText: Links between m objects of A and n objects of B in a many-to-many association <= m × n

title: Four visibility types
description: Larman's four ways an object can hold a reference to another object so that it can send it a message.
plainText: Visibility of B to A is one of: attribute, parameter, local, global

title: Weighted methods per class
description: CK metric summing the complexities of all methods of a class; with c_i = 1 it equals the number of methods.

title: Depth of inheritance tree
description: Number of generalisation links from a class up to the root of its hierarchy; deep trees raise reuse but also complexity.

title: Multiplicity to collection
description: A to-many association end is implemented as a List, Set or Map attribute rather than a single reference.

title: Availability
description: Fraction of time a system is operational; good exception handling and recovery lower MTTR and raise availability.

title: Complexity added by handlers
description: Each catch clause adds an alternative path, so a method with two ifs and one catch has V(G) = 4 by this counting.

title: Java throwable hierarchy
description: Error and RuntimeException subtrees are unchecked; every other Exception subclass is checked.

title: Cyclomatic complexity
description: E edges, N nodes and P connected components of the control-flow graph; equals the number of independent paths.

title: Basic COCOMO
description: Effort in person-months and duration in months, with constants chosen by organic, semi-detached or embedded mode.

title: Adjusted function points
description: The 14 general system characteristics Fi, each rated 0–5, adjust the unadjusted count by ±35%.

title: Defect removal efficiency
description: E errors found before delivery and D defects found after delivery.

title: Availability
description: MTTF + MTTR is the mean time between failures; availability is the fraction of time the system is up.

title: Mean time between failures
description: Average cycle length: mean time the system runs before failing plus the mean time taken to repair it.

title: Availability
description: Fraction of time the software is operational and available for use.

title: Reliability (constant failure rate)
description: Probability of failure-free operation for time t when failures occur at constant rate lambda = 1/MTTF.

title: Defect density
description: Number of defects found per thousand lines of code, a basic quality indicator.

title: Coupling ordering
description: Ranks module interdependence from the most desirable (data) to the least desirable (content).
plainText: Coupling best to worst: Data > Stamp > Control > External > Common > Content

title: Cohesion ordering
description: Ranks how strongly the elements inside one module belong together, best first.
plainText: Cohesion best to worst: Functional > Sequential > Communicational > Procedural > Temporal > Logical > Coincidental

title: Henry-Kafura information flow
description: Structural complexity metric that grows sharply with a module's fan-in and fan-out, weighted by its size.

title: Card-Glass structural complexity
description: Card and Glass define the structural complexity of module i as the square of its fan-out.

title: Phase defect removal efficiency
description: Measures how well a phase or test level filters its own errors before they escape to the next phase.

title: Requirements test coverage
description: Shows what share of the SRS is traced to at least one system or acceptance test.
plainText: Requirements coverage = requirements with tests / total requirements x 100%

title: Test pass rate
description: A simple progress indicator reported at each test level and for each regression run.
plainText: Pass rate = tests passed / tests executed x 100%

title: Anatomy of an object
description: Every object has attribute values (state), operations (behaviour) and a unique identity independent of its state.

title: Weighted methods per class (CK)
description: Sum of the complexities of a class's methods; with unit complexity it equals the method count, and high values suggest a class that is hard to reuse.

title: Depth of inheritance tree and number of children
description: Deeper DIT means more inherited behaviour and higher complexity; larger NOC means more reuse but more classes affected by a change.
latex: DIT(C) = \text{edges from root to } C,\quad NOC(C) = \text{immediate subclasses}
plainText: DIT(C) = edges from root to C; NOC(C) = number of immediate subclasses

title: System operations from SSDs
description: Every input event an actor sends to the black-box system on an SSD becomes a system operation that the design must implement.
latex: \text{System operations} = \text{distinct input events on the SSDs}
plainText: System operations = distinct input system events drawn on the SSDs

title: Operation contract sections
description: A Larman operation contract names the operation and its use cases, then states what must hold before and what state changes hold after.
plainText: Operation contract = Operation + Cross references + Preconditions + Postconditions

title: Analysis-to-design pipeline
description: The order in which use cases are elaborated into design artefacts within one iteration.
plainText: Use case text -> SSD -> operation contracts -> interaction diagrams -> design class diagram

title: Statement coverage
description: Share of source statements executed at least once by the unit tests written during test-first development.

title: Cyclomatic complexity of a method
description: Minimum number of unit tests needed to cover every independent path of a method; high values signal a candidate for Extract Method refactoring.
plainText: V(G) = E - N + 2P = number of decisions + 1

title: TDD cycle
description: Write a failing test, make it pass with the simplest code, then clean up while all tests stay green.

title: Agent composition
description: An agent is the agent program running on an architecture that supplies the physical sensors and actuators.

title: Agent function
description: The agent function maps every possible percept sequence to the action the agent takes.

title: Table-driven agent size
description: A lookup-table agent with |P| possible percepts over a lifetime of T steps needs one entry for every percept sequence of length 1 to T.

title: Expected utility
description: A utility-based agent scores each action by averaging the utility of its possible outcome states weighted by their probabilities.

title: Maximum expected utility choice
description: The rational utility-based agent selects the action with the highest expected utility.

title: Model-based state update
description: A model-based agent combines its previous internal state, last action, new percept and world model to estimate the current state.
